**Mason** is an [unincorporated community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unincorporated_area "Unincorporated area") in [Grant County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_County,_Kentucky "Grant County, Kentucky"), [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky"), United States.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason,_Grant_County,_Kentucky#cite_note-gnis-1) The community is located along [U.S. Route 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_25_(Kentucky) "U.S. Route 25 (Kentucky)")4.5 miles (7.2 km) south-southwest of [Williamstown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamstown,_Kentucky "Williamstown, Kentucky"). Mason has a [post office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_office "Post office") with [ZIP code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZIP_code "ZIP code") 41054, which opened on July 26, 1855.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason,_Grant_County,_Kentucky#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason,_Grant_County,_Kentucky#cite_note-3)

**Mason** is an [unincorporated community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unincorporated_area "Unincorporated area") in [Grant County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_County,_Kentucky "Grant County, Kentucky"), [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky "Kentucky"), United States.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason,_Grant_County,_Kentucky#cite_note-gnis-1) The community is located along [U.S. Route 25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_25_(Kentucky) "U.S. Route 25 (Kentucky)")4.5 miles (7.2 km) south-southwest of [Williamstown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williamstown,_Kentucky "Williamstown, Kentucky"). Mason has a [post office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_office "Post office") with [ZIP code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZIP_code "ZIP code") 41054, which opened on July 26, 1855.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason,_Grant_County,_Kentucky#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason,_Grant_County,_Kentucky#cite_note-3)

**St. Joseph** is a city in and the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") of [Buchanan County, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buchanan_County,_Missouri "Buchanan County, Missouri"), United States.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-GR6-4) Located on the [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River"), it is the principal city of the [St. Joseph Metropolitan Statistical Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_Metropolitan_Statistical_Area "St. Joseph Metropolitan Statistical Area"), which includes [Buchanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buchanan_County,_Missouri "Buchanan County, Missouri"), [Andrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_County,_Missouri "Andrew County, Missouri"), and [DeKalb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeKalb_County,_Missouri "DeKalb County, Missouri") counties in Missouri and [Doniphan County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doniphan_County,_Kansas "Doniphan County, Kansas"), [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas "Kansas"). As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), St. Joseph had a population of 72,473,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020PLLede-5) making it the [8th most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Missouri "List of cities in Missouri") in the state, and the 3rd most populous in Northwest Missouri.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-census-6) St. Joseph is located roughly 30 miles (48 km) north of the [Kansas City, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri") city limits and approximately 125 miles (201 km) south of [Omaha, Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omaha,_Nebraska "Omaha, Nebraska").

The city was named after the town's founder [Joseph Robidoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Robidoux_IV "Joseph Robidoux IV") and the biblical [Saint Joseph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Joseph "Saint Joseph").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-7) In the nineteenth century, it was the death place of American outlaw [Jesse James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_James "Jesse James"). It was also the starting point of the [Pony Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pony_Express "Pony Express") serving the West. Today, St. Joseph is home to [Missouri Western State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Western_State_University "Missouri Western State University"), which enrolls over 3,800 students.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-8)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/St_Joseph_Missouri_Francis.jpg/250px-St_Joseph_Missouri_Francis.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:St_Joseph_Missouri_Francis.jpg)

The intersection of Francis and North 4th streets in downtown St. Joseph

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/St_Joseph_Missouri_River.jpg/250px-St_Joseph_Missouri_River.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:St_Joseph_Missouri_River.jpg)

The [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River") in St. Joseph

St. Joseph was founded on the Missouri River by [Joseph Robidoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Robidoux_IV "Joseph Robidoux IV"), a local [fur trader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fur_trader "Fur trader") of French Canadian descent. It was officially incorporated in 1843.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-travel-9) In its early days, it was a bustling outpost and rough frontier town, serving as a last supply point and jumping-off point for travelers on the Missouri River toward the ["Wild West"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Old_West "American Old West"). It was the westernmost point in the United States accessible by rail until after the [American Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War"), which helped earn it the designation "Gateway to the West."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-10)

The main east–west downtown streets were named for Robidoux's eight children: Faraon, Jules, Francois (Francis), Felix, Edmond, Charles, Sylvanie, and Messanie. The street between Sylvanie and Messanie was named for his second wife, Angelique.

St. Joseph, or "St. Joe", as it was called by many, was a "Jumping-Off Point" for those migrants headed to the [Oregon Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_Territory "Oregon Territory") in the mid-1800s. Such cities, including [Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence,_Missouri "Independence, Missouri"), and St. Joseph, were where pioneers would stay and purchase supplies before they headed out in wagon trains across the Great Plains. The town was a very lively place.

Between April 3, 1860, and late October 1861, St. Joseph was one of the two endpoints of the [Pony Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pony_Express "Pony Express"), which operated for a short period over the land then inaccessible by rail, to provide fast mail service. Today the [Pony Express Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pony_Express_Museum "Pony Express Museum") hosts visitors in the former stables of the company. St. Joseph is identified by the slogan, "Where the Pony Express started and Jesse James ended."

The town's main hotel was [Patee House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patee_House "Patee House"). In the post-Civil War years, when the economy was down, the hotel was used for a time by the Patee Female College. It was occupied by the [St. Joseph Female College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_Female_College "St. Joseph Female College") up to 1880.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-11)

In 1874 the State Lunatic Asylum #2[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-12) was opened just East of St. Joseph. The asylum, originally built for 250 patients, opened its doors with more than 300. The asylum was mostly self-sustaining with three large farms, power plant, fire department, metal shops, wood shops, dairy and more, all worked by the patients. Over the decades the asylum grew rapidly, reaching its peak of close to 3,000 patients by the 1940s. In 1968 occupational therapist George Glore, with the help of his patients, recreated several historic treatment devices for Mental Health Awareness Month. This was the start of the [Glore Psychiatric Museum](https://www.stjosephmuseum.org/glore-psychiatric-museum). Now the largest museum of its kind in the world, the museum shows the history mental health treatment and still houses the original exhibits created by George Glore and his patients.

Outlaw [Jesse James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_James "Jesse James") lived here under the alias "Mr. Howard". The song, "[Jesse James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_James_(folk_song) "Jesse James (folk song)")", includes the lines, "...that dirty little coward that shot Mr. Howard has laid poor Jesse in his grave."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-william-13) On April 3, 1882, James was killed at his home, originally located at 1318 Lafayette. It has been relocated next to the Patee House and still has the visible bullet hole from the fatal shot. It is now operated as the [Jesse James Home Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_James_Home_Museum "Jesse James Home Museum").

The Heaton-Bowman-Smith Funeral Home maintains a small museum about Jesse James. Their predecessors conducted his funeral.

St. Joseph was the second city in the US to install electric streetcars; regular service was initiated on July 4, 1888.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-14) Among properties listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places") are [Robidoux Row](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robidoux_Row "Robidoux Row"), buildings owned by the founder and used for his family trading and mercantile business; the Patee House, now serving as a museum displaying St. Joseph's history, and the [Missouri Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Theater_and_Missouri_Theater_Building "Missouri Theater and Missouri Theater Building"), an ornate movie palace. The [Walnut Park Farm Historic District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walnut_Park_Farm_Historic_District "Walnut Park Farm Historic District") near St. Joseph was listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places") in 1999.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-nris-15)

St. Joseph's population peaked in 1900, with a census population of 102,979. This population figure is questionable, as civic leaders were known to have tried to raise the numbers for that census.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-bigcensus-16) At the time, Saint Joseph was home to one of the largest wholesale companies in the Midwest, the [Nave & McCord Mercantile Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nave_&_McCord_Mercantile_Company "Nave & McCord Mercantile Company"), as well as the [Hannibal and St. Joseph Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannibal_and_St._Joseph_Railroad "Hannibal and St. Joseph Railroad"), and the C.D. Smith & Company. C.D. Smith later became C.D. Smith Healthcare.

Prior to 1954 and desegregation, Bartlett High School served St. Joseph's African American students. It became Horace Mann Elementary with desegregation. You can learn about the Bartlett School at the [Black Archives Museum of St. Joseph](https://www.stjosephmuseum.org/black-archives-museum).[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-x798-17) St. Joseph's African American community leaders and [Nathaniel C. Bruce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathaniel_C._Bruce "Nathaniel C. Bruce") were involved in and supported the establishment of [Bartlett Agricultural and Industrial School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bartlett_Agricultural_and_Industrial_School "Bartlett Agricultural and Industrial School") in [Dalton, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalton,_Missouri "Dalton, Missouri"). It was modeled after [Tuskegee Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuskegee_Institute "Tuskegee Institute") and [Hampton Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hampton_Institute "Hampton Institute").

Saint Joseph is located on the Missouri/[Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas "Kansas") border in northwestern Missouri, also close to Nebraska; [Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa "Iowa") is another 70 miles (110 km) farther north. The nearest major metropolitan area to St. Joseph is the [Kansas City Metropolitan Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Metropolitan_Area "Kansas City Metropolitan Area"), which begins approximately 30 miles (48 km) to the south. The nearest major airport is [Kansas City International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_International_Airport "Kansas City International Airport"), which is approximately 35 miles (56 km) to the south. According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the city has a total area of 44.77 square miles (115.95 km 2), of which 43.99 square miles (113.93 km 2) is land and 0.78 square miles (2.02 km 2) is water.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-Gazetteer_files-18)

Several water bodies and streams are located in St. Joseph besides the Missouri River. [Roys Branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roys_Branch "Roys Branch") sources just northwest of [Krug Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krug_Park_(St._Joseph,_Missouri) "Krug Park (St. Joseph, Missouri)") and travels southwest and enters the Missouri River next to Remington Nature Center. Whitehead Creek headwaters southeast of St. Joseph and flows northwest into the Missouri River just southwest of downtown. Corby Pond, a public lake in Corby Park, is a popular fishing location. [Lake Contrary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Contrary "Lake Contrary") is located just southwest of St. Joseph and has a beach.

Under the [Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification"), St. Joseph has a [humid subtropical climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate "Humid subtropical climate") (_Cfa_) bordering on a [humid continental climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_continental_climate "Humid continental climate") (_Dfa_), although under United States isotherms of 32°F (0°C) the station is firmly continental. The monthly weather averages listed below are taken from National Weather Service 1981–2010 normals recorded at Rosecrans Airport. Because of the airport's location near the Missouri River and at a low elevation, official overnight lows during wintertime especially are often several degrees colder than at other places within the city.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-19) Snowfall is not recorded at the St. Joseph weather station although surrounding reporting stations typically receive 12 to 20 inches (0.30 to 0.51 meters) of snowfall annually.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-22)

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), St. Joseph had a population of 72,473 and 29,051 households; there were 16,841 families. The population density was 1,645.6 per square mile (635.4/km 2). The median age was 38.0 years. 22.2% of residents were under the age of 18 and 17.1% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 99.9 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 97.8 males age 18 and over.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DP-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020PL-28)

99.0% of residents lived in urban areas, while 1.0% lived in rural areas.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DHC-29)

There were 29,051 households in St. Joseph, of which 28.2% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 38.2% were married-couple households, 21.1% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 31.1% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 33.4% of all households were made up of individuals and 14.1% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DP-27)

There were 33,028 housing units, of which 12.0% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 2.5% and the rental vacancy rate was 12.9%.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DP-27)

### 2016–2020 American Community Survey

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2016–2020 American Community Survey")]

The 2016–2020 5-year [American Community Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Community_Survey "American Community Survey")[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-30) estimates show that the median household income was $48,716 (with a margin of error of +/- $2,421) and the median family income was $60,272 (+/- $2,679). Males had a median income of $34,486 (+/- $1,611) versus $25,623 (+/- $1,474) for females. The median income for those above 16 years old was $30,229 (+/- $1,494). Approximately, 12.0% of families and 16.9% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 23.9% of those under the age of 18 and 7.9% of those ages 65 or over.

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census") of 2010,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-wwwcensusgov-31) there were 76,780 people, 29,727 households, and 18,492 families residing in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 1,745.4 inhabitants per square mile (673.9/km 2). There were 33,189 housing units at an average density of 754.5 per square mile (291.3/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 87.8% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 6.0% Black, 0.5% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 0.9% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.2% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), 2.0% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), and 2.7% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") people of any race were 5.7% of the population.

There were 29,727 households, of which 32.0% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 42.0% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 14.5% had a female householder with no husband present, 5.7% had a male householder with no wife present, and 37.8% were non-families. 30.7% of all households were made up of individuals, and 12.2% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.43 and the average family size was 3.01.

In the city, the population was spread out, with 23.6% under the age of 18; 11.7% between the ages of 18 and 24; 26.1% from 25 to 44; 24.9% from 45 to 64; and 13.8% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age in the city was 35.6 years. The gender makeup of the city was 49.8% male and 50.2% female.

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the census[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-GR2-32) of 2000, there were 73,990 people, 29,026 households, and 18,460 families residing in the city. The population density was 1,687.7 people per square mile (651.6 people/km 2). There were 31,752 housing units at an average density of 724.2 per square mile (279.6/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 91.9% White, 5.0% Black, 0.5% Native American, 0.5% Asian, <0.1% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander_(U.S._Census) "Pacific Islander (U.S. Census)"), 0.7% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 1.4% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino of any race were 2.6% of the population.

There were 29,026 households, out of which 30.1% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 46.7% were married couples living together, 12.8% had a female householder with no husband present, and 36.4% were single-family households. 30.4% of all households were made up of individuals, and 13.2% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.39 and the average family size was 2.98.

In the city, the population was spread out, with 24.1% under the age of 18, 11.6% from 18 to 24, 28.6% from 25 to 44, 20.3% from 45 to 64, and 15.4% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 36 years. For every 100 females, there were 95.6 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 92.7 males.

The median income for a household in the city was $32,663, and the median income for a family was $40,995. Males had a median income of $31,300 versus $21,592 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the city was $17,445. About 9.1% of families and 13.0% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 15.5% of those under age 18 and 9.8% of those age 65 or over.

## Business

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Business")]

St. Joseph has a vibrant and diversified industrial economy making it the third largest exporter in Missouri.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-34) The industry includes major food processing, research, development, and production facilities of animal health products. Production of a wide range of heavy equipment, bio-fuels, meat and grains processing, candies, food processing equipment, metal can production, along with two major general contractors.

At the center of the so-called 'Kansas City Animal Health Corridor', which extends from Manhattan, Kansas, to Columbia, Missouri, St. Joseph is home to major animal health, pharmaceutical, nutrition research facilities. Including Boehringer Ingelheim [[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-35) and Nestle Purina.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-36)

Other agricultural products including herbicides for crop production and retail are produced in St. Joseph.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-37)

Herzog is based in St. Joseph. [TransitAmerica Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TransitAmerica_Services "TransitAmerica Services"), a subsidiary of Herzog, provides conductors and other railway technical positions for transit rail systems nationwide. Herzog Contracting, parent company to Transit America, is based in the city and provides construction services, rail equipment, rail testing, and signaling services to freight and transit systems throughout North America and the Caribbean.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-39)

St. Joseph has the third-largest manufacturing economy in Missouri, after St. Louis and Kansas City.

In June 2019, total employment in the St. Joseph Metropolitan Area was 65,099 persons.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-40)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Education")]

### Public schools

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Public schools")]

The vast majority of the city limits is in the [St. Joseph School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_School_District?action=edit&redlink=1 "St. Joseph School District (page does not exist)").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-CensusSDMap-42) The St. Joseph School District operates three public high schools, four public middle schools and 16 public elementary schools in St. Joseph. There are three private grade schools, a private high school and a private [K–12](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-12_education "K-12 education") Christian school. Two new elementary schools (Oak Grove and Carden Park) have been constructed, and both opened by the 2014–15 academic year. In addition, there is an active home education community that serves the city and surrounding areas. In [higher education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Higher_education "Higher education"), St. Joseph is the home of a regional [public university](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_university "Public university") as well as a public university outreach center, a public [technical school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technical_school "Technical school") and a private technical school.

### Library

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Library")]

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Free_Public_Library_at_St._Joseph%2C_Missouri.jpg/250px-Free_Public_Library_at_St._Joseph%2C_Missouri.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Free_Public_Library_at_St._Joseph,_Missouri.jpg)

Free Public Library at St. Joseph, Missouri

St. Joseph has a four-branch public library system.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-47) The system is overseen by the Library Board, which consists of nine members appointed by the mayor, with city council approval, for three-year terms.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-48) The [Downtown Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_Public_Library "St. Joseph Public Library"), located in downtown St. Joseph, houses the administrative offices for the library system.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-49)[Carnegie Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_Public_Library-Carnegie_Branch "St. Joseph Public Library-Carnegie Branch") and Washington Park Library are neighborhood branches that serve communities in the North and South ends of the city.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-51) East Hills Library is the largest branch, located off [Interstate 29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_29 "Interstate 29"), which serves the greater St. Joseph area.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-52) Downtown Library and Carnegie Library were listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places") in 1982 and 1990 respectively.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-53)

St. Joseph also has a branch of the Rolling Hills Consolidated Library. This library was founded in 1961 with its headquarters in the basement of the Washington Park Library. The library currently occupies over 23,000 square feet of space off of the Belt Highway. The space is used for the library itself, its administration offices, a used book store, and "The Upper Story", a large rentable meeting room.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-:0-54)

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Transportation")]

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/BN_Passenger_Trains_in_1970_and_1971_-_5_Roger_Puta_Photos_%2827393894566%29.jpg/330px-BN_Passenger_Trains_in_1970_and_1971_-_5_Roger_Puta_Photos_%2827393894566%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:BN_Passenger_Trains_in_1970_and_1971_-_5_Roger_Puta_Photos_(27393894566).jpg)

A Burlington Northern passenger train at St. Joseph in 1970

The [St. Joseph Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_Transit "St. Joseph Transit") is publicly owned and provides bus service. [Rosecrans Memorial Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosecrans_Memorial_Airport "Rosecrans Memorial Airport") is a joint municipal/military owned airport for general aviation. It is the home of the [139th Airlift Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/139th_Airlift_Wing "139th Airlift Wing") of the [Missouri Air National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Air_National_Guard "Missouri Air National Guard"), and does not have commercial service. The nearest commercial airport is [Kansas City International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_International_Airport "Kansas City International Airport"), which is approximately 35 miles (56 km) to the south. Intercity bus service to the city is provided by [Jefferson Lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Lines "Jefferson Lines").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-55)

Looking south at the I-229 viaduct and the Missouri River from Wyeth Hill

## Cityscape

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Cityscape")]

Numerous parks, golf courses, sports complexes, skate parks, a water park, a [riverwalk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedestrian_zone "Pedestrian zone") along the Missouri River, and a small conservation area can be found throughout St. Joseph proper. The city is also nationally known for its 26-mile (42 km)[parkway system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_Parkway "St. Joseph Parkway"), which is accompanied by an urban trail system.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-stjomo.com-56) Two of the city's largest parks are [Krug Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krug_Park_(St._Joseph,_Missouri) "Krug Park (St. Joseph, Missouri)") and Hyde Park; these respectively anchor the parkway and urban trail on the north and south. A [dog park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog_park "Dog park") has been added to the parkway system near Corby Pond.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-57) There are many buildings that were built early on in the city's history, one of which being the [Missouri Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Theater_(St._Joseph,_Missouri) "Missouri Theater (St. Joseph, Missouri)").

## Media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Media")]

St. Joseph currently ranks 201st largest [designated market area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Designated_market_area "Designated market area") out of 210 [media markets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_television_stations_in_North_America_by_media_market "List of television stations in North America by media market") in the United States (as ranked by [Nielsen Media Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_Media_Research "Nielsen Media Research")); the market covers six counties in northwestern Missouri ([Holt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holt_County,_Missouri "Holt County, Missouri"), [Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worth_County,_Missouri "Worth County, Missouri"), [Nodaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nodaway_County,_Missouri "Nodaway County, Missouri"), [Andrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_County,_Missouri "Andrew County, Missouri"), [DeKalb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeKalb_County,_Missouri "DeKalb County, Missouri") and [Buchanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buchanan_County,_Missouri "Buchanan County, Missouri")) and [Doniphan County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doniphan_County,_Kansas "Doniphan County, Kansas") in northeastern Kansas. The St. Joseph area has three low-power and two full-power television stations, and ten radio stations. News-Press & Gazette, a media corporation, is headquartered in Saint Joseph. They have interests in numerous television, radio, and newspaper markets throughout the midwestern and western United States.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-58)

### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Television")]

Due to its proximity to Kansas City, stations from that market serve as default affiliate of MyNetworkTV ([KSMO-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KSMO-TV "KSMO-TV")/Kansas City) and default member station of PBS ([KCPT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KCPT "KCPT")/Kansas City) due to the lack of stations of either network licensed to the market. [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") affiliate [KQTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KQTV "KQTV") had long been the only major commercial station in St. Joseph, but in June 2012, the locally based [News-Press & Gazette Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/News-Press_&_Gazette_Company "News-Press & Gazette Company") signed on [KNPN-LD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KNPN-LD "KNPN-LD") as a [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company") affiliate, KBJO-LD as a [CW+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW_Plus "The CW Plus") affiliate, and KNPG-LD as a [Telemundo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telemundo "Telemundo") affiliate. This in turn was followed by the conversions of KBJO-LD to [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") affiliate [KNPG-LD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KNPG-LD "KNPG-LD") in November 2016 (retaining the CW+ as a LD2 subchannel),[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-newspress-knpgnbc-59) and the original KNPG-LD (which assumed the KBJO-LD call letters) to [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") affiliate [KCJO-LD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KCJO-LD "KCJO-LD") in June 2017,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-cbsstjoe-60) ending out-of-market reliance for major network programming.

**St. Joseph** is a city in and the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") of [Buchanan County, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buchanan_County,_Missouri "Buchanan County, Missouri"), United States.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-GR6-4) Located on the [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River"), it is the principal city of the [St. Joseph Metropolitan Statistical Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_Metropolitan_Statistical_Area "St. Joseph Metropolitan Statistical Area"), which includes [Buchanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buchanan_County,_Missouri "Buchanan County, Missouri"), [Andrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_County,_Missouri "Andrew County, Missouri"), and [DeKalb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeKalb_County,_Missouri "DeKalb County, Missouri") counties in Missouri and [Doniphan County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doniphan_County,_Kansas "Doniphan County, Kansas"), [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas "Kansas"). As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), St. Joseph had a population of 72,473,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020PLLede-5) making it the [8th most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Missouri "List of cities in Missouri") in the state, and the 3rd most populous in Northwest Missouri.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-census-6) St. Joseph is located roughly 30 miles (48 km) north of the [Kansas City, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City,_Missouri "Kansas City, Missouri") city limits and approximately 125 miles (201 km) south of [Omaha, Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omaha,_Nebraska "Omaha, Nebraska").

The city was named after the town's founder [Joseph Robidoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Robidoux_IV "Joseph Robidoux IV") and the biblical [Saint Joseph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Joseph "Saint Joseph").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-7) In the nineteenth century, it was the death place of American outlaw [Jesse James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_James "Jesse James"). It was also the starting point of the [Pony Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pony_Express "Pony Express") serving the West. Today, St. Joseph is home to [Missouri Western State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Western_State_University "Missouri Western State University"), which enrolls over 3,800 students.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-8)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/St_Joseph_Missouri_Francis.jpg/250px-St_Joseph_Missouri_Francis.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:St_Joseph_Missouri_Francis.jpg)

The intersection of Francis and North 4th streets in downtown St. Joseph

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/St_Joseph_Missouri_River.jpg/250px-St_Joseph_Missouri_River.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:St_Joseph_Missouri_River.jpg)

The [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River") in St. Joseph

St. Joseph was founded on the Missouri River by [Joseph Robidoux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Robidoux_IV "Joseph Robidoux IV"), a local [fur trader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fur_trader "Fur trader") of French Canadian descent. It was officially incorporated in 1843.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-travel-9) In its early days, it was a bustling outpost and rough frontier town, serving as a last supply point and jumping-off point for travelers on the Missouri River toward the ["Wild West"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Old_West "American Old West"). It was the westernmost point in the United States accessible by rail until after the [American Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War"), which helped earn it the designation "Gateway to the West."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-10)

The main east–west downtown streets were named for Robidoux's eight children: Faraon, Jules, Francois (Francis), Felix, Edmond, Charles, Sylvanie, and Messanie. The street between Sylvanie and Messanie was named for his second wife, Angelique.

St. Joseph, or "St. Joe", as it was called by many, was a "Jumping-Off Point" for those migrants headed to the [Oregon Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_Territory "Oregon Territory") in the mid-1800s. Such cities, including [Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence,_Missouri "Independence, Missouri"), and St. Joseph, were where pioneers would stay and purchase supplies before they headed out in wagon trains across the Great Plains. The town was a very lively place.

Between April 3, 1860, and late October 1861, St. Joseph was one of the two endpoints of the [Pony Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pony_Express "Pony Express"), which operated for a short period over the land then inaccessible by rail, to provide fast mail service. Today the [Pony Express Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pony_Express_Museum "Pony Express Museum") hosts visitors in the former stables of the company. St. Joseph is identified by the slogan, "Where the Pony Express started and Jesse James ended."

The town's main hotel was [Patee House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patee_House "Patee House"). In the post-Civil War years, when the economy was down, the hotel was used for a time by the Patee Female College. It was occupied by the [St. Joseph Female College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_Female_College "St. Joseph Female College") up to 1880.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-11)

In 1874 the State Lunatic Asylum #2[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-12) was opened just East of St. Joseph. The asylum, originally built for 250 patients, opened its doors with more than 300. The asylum was mostly self-sustaining with three large farms, power plant, fire department, metal shops, wood shops, dairy and more, all worked by the patients. Over the decades the asylum grew rapidly, reaching its peak of close to 3,000 patients by the 1940s. In 1968 occupational therapist George Glore, with the help of his patients, recreated several historic treatment devices for Mental Health Awareness Month. This was the start of the [Glore Psychiatric Museum](https://www.stjosephmuseum.org/glore-psychiatric-museum). Now the largest museum of its kind in the world, the museum shows the history mental health treatment and still houses the original exhibits created by George Glore and his patients.

Outlaw [Jesse James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_James "Jesse James") lived here under the alias "Mr. Howard". The song, "[Jesse James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_James_(folk_song) "Jesse James (folk song)")", includes the lines, "...that dirty little coward that shot Mr. Howard has laid poor Jesse in his grave."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-william-13) On April 3, 1882, James was killed at his home, originally located at 1318 Lafayette. It has been relocated next to the Patee House and still has the visible bullet hole from the fatal shot. It is now operated as the [Jesse James Home Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_James_Home_Museum "Jesse James Home Museum").

The Heaton-Bowman-Smith Funeral Home maintains a small museum about Jesse James. Their predecessors conducted his funeral.

St. Joseph was the second city in the US to install electric streetcars; regular service was initiated on July 4, 1888.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-14) Among properties listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places") are [Robidoux Row](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robidoux_Row "Robidoux Row"), buildings owned by the founder and used for his family trading and mercantile business; the Patee House, now serving as a museum displaying St. Joseph's history, and the [Missouri Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Theater_and_Missouri_Theater_Building "Missouri Theater and Missouri Theater Building"), an ornate movie palace. The [Walnut Park Farm Historic District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walnut_Park_Farm_Historic_District "Walnut Park Farm Historic District") near St. Joseph was listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places") in 1999.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-nris-15)

St. Joseph's population peaked in 1900, with a census population of 102,979. This population figure is questionable, as civic leaders were known to have tried to raise the numbers for that census.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-bigcensus-16) At the time, Saint Joseph was home to one of the largest wholesale companies in the Midwest, the [Nave & McCord Mercantile Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nave_&_McCord_Mercantile_Company "Nave & McCord Mercantile Company"), as well as the [Hannibal and St. Joseph Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannibal_and_St._Joseph_Railroad "Hannibal and St. Joseph Railroad"), and the C.D. Smith & Company. C.D. Smith later became C.D. Smith Healthcare.

Prior to 1954 and desegregation, Bartlett High School served St. Joseph's African American students. It became Horace Mann Elementary with desegregation. You can learn about the Bartlett School at the [Black Archives Museum of St. Joseph](https://www.stjosephmuseum.org/black-archives-museum).[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-x798-17) St. Joseph's African American community leaders and [Nathaniel C. Bruce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathaniel_C._Bruce "Nathaniel C. Bruce") were involved in and supported the establishment of [Bartlett Agricultural and Industrial School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bartlett_Agricultural_and_Industrial_School "Bartlett Agricultural and Industrial School") in [Dalton, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalton,_Missouri "Dalton, Missouri"). It was modeled after [Tuskegee Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuskegee_Institute "Tuskegee Institute") and [Hampton Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hampton_Institute "Hampton Institute").

## Geography and climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography and climate")]

Downtown St. Joseph in 2006

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/63/St_Joseph_Missouri_skyline.jpg/330px-St_Joseph_Missouri_skyline.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:St_Joseph_Missouri_skyline.jpg)

Another view of the downtown in 2006

Saint Joseph is located on the Missouri/[Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas "Kansas") border in northwestern Missouri, also close to Nebraska; [Iowa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa "Iowa") is another 70 miles (110 km) farther north. The nearest major metropolitan area to St. Joseph is the [Kansas City Metropolitan Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_Metropolitan_Area "Kansas City Metropolitan Area"), which begins approximately 30 miles (48 km) to the south. The nearest major airport is [Kansas City International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_International_Airport "Kansas City International Airport"), which is approximately 35 miles (56 km) to the south. According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the city has a total area of 44.77 square miles (115.95 km 2), of which 43.99 square miles (113.93 km 2) is land and 0.78 square miles (2.02 km 2) is water.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-Gazetteer_files-18)

Several water bodies and streams are located in St. Joseph besides the Missouri River. [Roys Branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roys_Branch "Roys Branch") sources just northwest of [Krug Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krug_Park_(St._Joseph,_Missouri) "Krug Park (St. Joseph, Missouri)") and travels southwest and enters the Missouri River next to Remington Nature Center. Whitehead Creek headwaters southeast of St. Joseph and flows northwest into the Missouri River just southwest of downtown. Corby Pond, a public lake in Corby Park, is a popular fishing location. [Lake Contrary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Contrary "Lake Contrary") is located just southwest of St. Joseph and has a beach.

Under the [Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification"), St. Joseph has a [humid subtropical climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_subtropical_climate "Humid subtropical climate") (_Cfa_) bordering on a [humid continental climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_continental_climate "Humid continental climate") (_Dfa_), although under United States isotherms of 32°F (0°C) the station is firmly continental. The monthly weather averages listed below are taken from National Weather Service 1981–2010 normals recorded at Rosecrans Airport. Because of the airport's location near the Missouri River and at a low elevation, official overnight lows during wintertime especially are often several degrees colder than at other places within the city.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-19) Snowfall is not recorded at the St. Joseph weather station although surrounding reporting stations typically receive 12 to 20 inches (0.30 to 0.51 meters) of snowfall annually.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-22)

### 2016–2020 American Community Survey

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2016–2020 American Community Survey")]

The 2016–2020 5-year [American Community Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Community_Survey "American Community Survey")[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-30) estimates show that the median household income was $48,716 (with a margin of error of +/- $2,421) and the median family income was $60,272 (+/- $2,679). Males had a median income of $34,486 (+/- $1,611) versus $25,623 (+/- $1,474) for females. The median income for those above 16 years old was $30,229 (+/- $1,494). Approximately, 12.0% of families and 16.9% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 23.9% of those under the age of 18 and 7.9% of those ages 65 or over.

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census") of 2010,[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-wwwcensusgov-31) there were 76,780 people, 29,727 households, and 18,492 families residing in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 1,745.4 inhabitants per square mile (673.9/km 2). There were 33,189 housing units at an average density of 754.5 per square mile (291.3/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 87.8% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 6.0% Black, 0.5% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 0.9% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.2% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), 2.0% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), and 2.7% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") people of any race were 5.7% of the population.

There were 29,727 households, of which 32.0% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 42.0% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 14.5% had a female householder with no husband present, 5.7% had a male householder with no wife present, and 37.8% were non-families. 30.7% of all households were made up of individuals, and 12.2% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.43 and the average family size was 3.01.

In the city, the population was spread out, with 23.6% under the age of 18; 11.7% between the ages of 18 and 24; 26.1% from 25 to 44; 24.9% from 45 to 64; and 13.8% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age in the city was 35.6 years. The gender makeup of the city was 49.8% male and 50.2% female.

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

As of the census[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-GR2-32) of 2000, there were 73,990 people, 29,026 households, and 18,460 families residing in the city. The population density was 1,687.7 people per square mile (651.6 people/km 2). There were 31,752 housing units at an average density of 724.2 per square mile (279.6/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 91.9% White, 5.0% Black, 0.5% Native American, 0.5% Asian, <0.1% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander_(U.S._Census) "Pacific Islander (U.S. Census)"), 0.7% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 1.4% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino of any race were 2.6% of the population.

There were 29,026 households, out of which 30.1% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 46.7% were married couples living together, 12.8% had a female householder with no husband present, and 36.4% were single-family households. 30.4% of all households were made up of individuals, and 13.2% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.39 and the average family size was 2.98.

In the city, the population was spread out, with 24.1% under the age of 18, 11.6% from 18 to 24, 28.6% from 25 to 44, 20.3% from 45 to 64, and 15.4% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 36 years. For every 100 females, there were 95.6 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 92.7 males.

The median income for a household in the city was $32,663, and the median income for a family was $40,995. Males had a median income of $31,300 versus $21,592 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the city was $17,445. About 9.1% of families and 13.0% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 15.5% of those under age 18 and 9.8% of those age 65 or over.

## Business

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Business")]

St. Joseph has a vibrant and diversified industrial economy making it the third largest exporter in Missouri.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-34) The industry includes major food processing, research, development, and production facilities of animal health products. Production of a wide range of heavy equipment, bio-fuels, meat and grains processing, candies, food processing equipment, metal can production, along with two major general contractors.

At the center of the so-called 'Kansas City Animal Health Corridor', which extends from Manhattan, Kansas, to Columbia, Missouri, St. Joseph is home to major animal health, pharmaceutical, nutrition research facilities. Including Boehringer Ingelheim [[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-35) and Nestle Purina.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-36)

Other agricultural products including herbicides for crop production and retail are produced in St. Joseph.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-37)

Herzog is based in St. Joseph. [TransitAmerica Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TransitAmerica_Services "TransitAmerica Services"), a subsidiary of Herzog, provides conductors and other railway technical positions for transit rail systems nationwide. Herzog Contracting, parent company to Transit America, is based in the city and provides construction services, rail equipment, rail testing, and signaling services to freight and transit systems throughout North America and the Caribbean.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-39)

St. Joseph has the third-largest manufacturing economy in Missouri, after St. Louis and Kansas City.

In June 2019, total employment in the St. Joseph Metropolitan Area was 65,099 persons.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-40)

### Public schools

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Public schools")]

### Library

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Library")]

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Free_Public_Library_at_St._Joseph%2C_Missouri.jpg/250px-Free_Public_Library_at_St._Joseph%2C_Missouri.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Free_Public_Library_at_St._Joseph,_Missouri.jpg)

Free Public Library at St. Joseph, Missouri

St. Joseph has a four-branch public library system.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-47) The system is overseen by the Library Board, which consists of nine members appointed by the mayor, with city council approval, for three-year terms.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-48) The [Downtown Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_Public_Library "St. Joseph Public Library"), located in downtown St. Joseph, houses the administrative offices for the library system.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-49)[Carnegie Library](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_Public_Library-Carnegie_Branch "St. Joseph Public Library-Carnegie Branch") and Washington Park Library are neighborhood branches that serve communities in the North and South ends of the city.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-51) East Hills Library is the largest branch, located off [Interstate 29](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_29 "Interstate 29"), which serves the greater St. Joseph area.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-52) Downtown Library and Carnegie Library were listed on the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places") in 1982 and 1990 respectively.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-53)

St. Joseph also has a branch of the Rolling Hills Consolidated Library. This library was founded in 1961 with its headquarters in the basement of the Washington Park Library. The library currently occupies over 23,000 square feet of space off of the Belt Highway. The space is used for the library itself, its administration offices, a used book store, and "The Upper Story", a large rentable meeting room.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-:0-54)

The [St. Joseph Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_Transit "St. Joseph Transit") is publicly owned and provides bus service. [Rosecrans Memorial Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosecrans_Memorial_Airport "Rosecrans Memorial Airport") is a joint municipal/military owned airport for general aviation. It is the home of the [139th Airlift Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/139th_Airlift_Wing "139th Airlift Wing") of the [Missouri Air National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Air_National_Guard "Missouri Air National Guard"), and does not have commercial service. The nearest commercial airport is [Kansas City International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_City_International_Airport "Kansas City International Airport"), which is approximately 35 miles (56 km) to the south. Intercity bus service to the city is provided by [Jefferson Lines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_Lines "Jefferson Lines").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-55)

## Cityscape

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Cityscape")]

Numerous parks, golf courses, sports complexes, skate parks, a water park, a [riverwalk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedestrian_zone "Pedestrian zone") along the Missouri River, and a small conservation area can be found throughout St. Joseph proper. The city is also nationally known for its 26-mile (42 km)[parkway system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_Parkway "St. Joseph Parkway"), which is accompanied by an urban trail system.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-stjomo.com-56) Two of the city's largest parks are [Krug Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krug_Park_(St._Joseph,_Missouri) "Krug Park (St. Joseph, Missouri)") and Hyde Park; these respectively anchor the parkway and urban trail on the north and south. A [dog park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog_park "Dog park") has been added to the parkway system near Corby Pond.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-57) There are many buildings that were built early on in the city's history, one of which being the [Missouri Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Theater_(St._Joseph,_Missouri) "Missouri Theater (St. Joseph, Missouri)").

## Media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Media")]

St. Joseph currently ranks 201st largest [designated market area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Designated_market_area "Designated market area") out of 210 [media markets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_television_stations_in_North_America_by_media_market "List of television stations in North America by media market") in the United States (as ranked by [Nielsen Media Research](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nielsen_Media_Research "Nielsen Media Research")); the market covers six counties in northwestern Missouri ([Holt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holt_County,_Missouri "Holt County, Missouri"), [Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worth_County,_Missouri "Worth County, Missouri"), [Nodaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nodaway_County,_Missouri "Nodaway County, Missouri"), [Andrew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_County,_Missouri "Andrew County, Missouri"), [DeKalb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeKalb_County,_Missouri "DeKalb County, Missouri") and [Buchanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buchanan_County,_Missouri "Buchanan County, Missouri")) and [Doniphan County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doniphan_County,_Kansas "Doniphan County, Kansas") in northeastern Kansas. The St. Joseph area has three low-power and two full-power television stations, and ten radio stations. News-Press & Gazette, a media corporation, is headquartered in Saint Joseph. They have interests in numerous television, radio, and newspaper markets throughout the midwestern and western United States.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-58)

### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Joseph,_Missouri&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Television")]

Due to its proximity to Kansas City, stations from that market serve as default affiliate of MyNetworkTV ([KSMO-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KSMO-TV "KSMO-TV")/Kansas City) and default member station of PBS ([KCPT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KCPT "KCPT")/Kansas City) due to the lack of stations of either network licensed to the market. [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") affiliate [KQTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KQTV "KQTV") had long been the only major commercial station in St. Joseph, but in June 2012, the locally based [News-Press & Gazette Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/News-Press_&_Gazette_Company "News-Press & Gazette Company") signed on [KNPN-LD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KNPN-LD "KNPN-LD") as a [Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Broadcasting_Company "Fox Broadcasting Company") affiliate, KBJO-LD as a [CW+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_CW_Plus "The CW Plus") affiliate, and KNPG-LD as a [Telemundo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telemundo "Telemundo") affiliate. This in turn was followed by the conversions of KBJO-LD to [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") affiliate [KNPG-LD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KNPG-LD "KNPG-LD") in November 2016 (retaining the CW+ as a LD2 subchannel),[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-newspress-knpgnbc-59) and the original KNPG-LD (which assumed the KBJO-LD call letters) to [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") affiliate [KCJO-LD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KCJO-LD "KCJO-LD") in June 2017,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph,_Missouri#cite_note-cbsstjoe-60) ending out-of-market reliance for major network programming.

**Saint Charles** (commonly abbreviated **St. Charles**) is a city in and the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") of [St. Charles County, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri "St. Charles County, Missouri"), United States.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-GR6-2) The population was 70,493 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), making St. Charles the [eighth-most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Missouri "List of cities in Missouri") in [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"). Situated on the [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River") near its mouth at the [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_River "Mississippi River"), St. Charles is approximately 20 miles northwest of St. Louis.

The city was founded circa 1769 as Les Petites Côtes, or "The Little Hillsides" in French, by [Louis Blanchette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Blanchette "Louis Blanchette"), a French-Canadian fur trader.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-3) The St. Charles area was settled primarily by French-speaking colonists from Canada in its early days. This former [French territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Country "Illinois Country") west of the Mississippi River was nominally ruled [by Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Louisiana "Spanish Louisiana") following France's defeat in the [Seven Years' War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Years'_War "Seven Years' War"), while France had also ceded the east of the Mississippi to Great Britain. St. Charles is thus the third-oldest city in what is now the state of [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"). In the 18th and 19th century, the city's waterfront played a significant role as a river port for westward trade and expansion, including trade with Native American tribes on the upper Missouri River.

In 1804, the [Lewis and Clark Expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_and_Clark_Expedition "Lewis and Clark Expedition") considered this settlement the last "civilized" stop before they headed upriver to explore the western territory that the United States acquired from France in the [Louisiana Purchase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Purchase "Louisiana Purchase").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-4)

The city served as the first Missouri capital from 1821 to 1826.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-5) It was also the starting point of the [Boone's Lick Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boone's_Lick_Road "Boone's Lick Road") to the [Boonslick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boonslick "Boonslick") and the [Santa Fe Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Trail "Santa Fe Trail"). In the 20th century, it became the site of the [Saint Rose Philippine Duchesne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Rose_Philippine_Duchesne "Saint Rose Philippine Duchesne") Catholic shrine.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-6)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") peoples inhabited the area at least as early as 11,000 B.C. When European colonists arrived, the area was inhabited by the historic Ilini, Osage and Missouri tribes.

According to Hopewell's _Legends of the Missouri and Mississippi_, Blanchette met another French Canadian (Bernard Guillet) at this site in 1765. Blanchette, determined to settle there, asked if Guillet, who had become an honorary chief of a [Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakota_people "Lakota people") band, had chosen a name for it.

"I called the place 'Les Petites Côtes' " replied Bernard, "from the sides of the hills that you see.""By that name shall it be called", said Blanchette Chasseur, "for it is the echo of nature—beautiful from its simplicity."
Blanchette settled there _circa_ 1769 under the authority of the Spanish governor of [Upper Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Louisiana "Upper Louisiana") (the area had been ceded by France [to Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Louisiana "Spanish Louisiana") under an agreement with Great Britain following French defeat in the [French and Indian Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_and_Indian_Wars "French and Indian Wars")). He was appointed as the territory's civil and military leader, serving until his death in 1793. Although the settlement was under Spanish jurisdiction, the settlers were primarily Native American and French Canadians who had migrated from northern territories and most of whom spoke French.

Considered to begin in St. Charles, the [Boone's Lick Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boone's_Lick_Road "Boone's Lick Road") along the Missouri River was the major overland route for European-American settlement of central and western Missouri. This area became known as the [Boonslick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boonslick "Boonslick") or "Boonslick Country." At [Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin,_Missouri "Franklin, Missouri"), the trail ended.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-7) Westward progress continued on the [Santa Fe Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Trail "Santa Fe Trail").

### San Carlos Borromeo

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: San Carlos Borromeo")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Sacred_Heart_Convent_and_Saint_Charles_Borromeo_Catholic_Church_in_Saint_Charles.jpg/330px-Sacred_Heart_Convent_and_Saint_Charles_Borromeo_Catholic_Church_in_Saint_Charles.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sacred_Heart_Convent_and_Saint_Charles_Borromeo_Catholic_Church_in_Saint_Charles.jpg)

Sacred Heart Convent and Saint Charles Borromeo Catholic Church, 1908

The first church, built in 1791, was Catholic and dedicated to the Italian saint [Charles Borromeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Borromeo "Charles Borromeo"), under the Spanish version of his name, San Carlos Borromeo. The town became known as San Carlos del Misuri (St. Charles of the Missouri). The original location of the church is not known but a replica has been built just off Main Street. The fourth St. Charles Borromeo Church now stands on Fifth Street.

The Spanish Lieutenant-Governor [Carlos de Hault de Lassus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_de_Hault_de_Lassus "Carlos de Hault de Lassus") appointed [Daniel Boone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Boone "Daniel Boone") as commandant of the [Femme Osage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femme_Osage?action=edit&redlink=1 "Femme Osage (page does not exist)") District. He served in this role until the United States government acquired control in 1804 following the [Louisiana Purchase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Purchase "Louisiana Purchase") from France.

The name of the town, San Carlos, was anglicized to St. Charles. [William Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Clark_(explorer) "William Clark (explorer)") arrived in St. Charles on May 16, 1804. With him were 40 men and three boats; they made final preparations for their major cross-country expedition, as they waited for [Meriwether Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meriwether_Lewis "Meriwether Lewis") to arrive from St. Louis. They attended dances, dinners, and a church service during this time. Excited to be part of the national expedition, the townspeople were very hospitable to the explorers. Lewis arrived via [St. Charles Rock Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Rock_Road "St. Charles Rock Road") on May 20. The expedition launched the next day in a [keel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keel "Keel") boat at 3:30 pm. St. Charles was the last established European-American town that the expedition visited for more than two and a half years.

### State capital and growth

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: State capital and growth")]

When Missouri was granted statehood in 1821, the legislature decided to build a "City of [Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson")" to serve as the state capital, in the center of the state, overlooking the Missouri River. Since this land was undeveloped at the time, a temporary capital was needed. St. Charles was chosen over eight other cities in a competition to house the temporary capital. It offered free meeting space for the legislature in rooms located above a hardware store. This building is preserved as the [First Missouri State Capitol State Historic Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Missouri_State_Capitol_State_Historic_Site "First Missouri State Capitol State Historic Site") and may be toured. The Missouri government continued to meet there until buildings were completed in [Jefferson City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_City,_Missouri "Jefferson City, Missouri") in 1826.

[Gottfried Duden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gottfried_Duden "Gottfried Duden") was a German who visited in the area in 1824. Travelling under the guidance of Daniel M. Boone, he wrote extensive accounts of life in [St. Charles County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri "St. Charles County, Missouri") during his year there. He published these after returning to Germany in 1829, and his favorable impressions of the area led to the immigration of a number of Germans in 1833. The first permanent German settler in the region was probably Louis Eversman, who had arrived with Duden but decided to stay.

In the post-World War II era, the federal government undertook a major program of interstate highway construction. St. Charles is where the first claimed interstate project was started in 1956. A state highway marker is displayed with a logo and information regarding this claim, off Interstate 70 going westbound, to the right of the First Capitol Drive exit.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Kansas and Pennsylvania also claim to have had the first interstate project.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-8)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Geography")]

St. Charles is located about 20 miles northwest of St. Louis. According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the city has a total area of 24.03 square miles (62.24 km 2), of which 23.65 square miles (61.25 km 2) is land and 0.38 square miles (0.98 km 2) is water.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-Gazetteer_files-9)

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Climate")]

St. Charles has a Köppen humid subtropical climate, with warm and humid summers (eventual hot days) and cool winters (with short cold spells possible sometimes). Precipitation is mostly light to moderate, with occasional stormy weather. Spring is the wettest season on average.
