### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), St. Charles had a population of 70,493. The population density was 2,800.7 per square mile (1,081.3/km 2).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DP-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020PL-14)

The median age was 38.8 years. 18.7% of residents were under the age of 18 and 17.8% of residents were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 95.0 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 93.0 males age 18 and over.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DP-13)

99.9% of residents lived in urban areas, while 0.1% lived in rural areas.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DHC-15)

There were 29,863 households and 16,791 families in St. Charles, of which 24.4% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 44.1% were married-couple households, 20.3% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 28.0% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 32.9% of all households were made up of individuals and 12.1% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.2 and the average family size was 2.9.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DP-13)

There were 31,744 housing units, of which 5.9% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.9% and the rental vacancy rate was 7.9%.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DP-13)

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-wwwcensusgov-17) of 2010, there were 65,794 people, 26,715 households, and 16,128 families residing in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 2,782.0 inhabitants per square mile (1,074.1/km 2). There were 28,590 housing units at an average density of 1,208.9 per square mile (466.8/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 87.5% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 5.9% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 0.3% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 2.5% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.1% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), 1.8% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), and 1.9% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 4.2% of the population.

There were 26,715 households, of which 27.5% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 45.4% were married couples living together, 10.8% had a female householder with no husband present, 4.2% had a male householder with no wife present, and 39.6% were non-families. 31.9% of all households were made up of individuals, and 10.1% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.29 and the average family size was 2.90.

The median age in the city was 36.6 years. 19.7% of residents were under the age of 18; 13.8% were between the ages of 18 and 24; 25.9% were from 25 to 44; 26.6% were from 45 to 64; and 13.9% were 65 years of age or older. The gender makeup of the city was 49.0% male and 51.0% female.

According to 2014, American Community Survey 5-year Estimates the median income for a household in the city was $56,622, and the median income for a family was $73,234. Males had a median income of $51,477 versus $40,311 females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the city was $29,645. 8.8% of families and 11.5% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 18.7% of those under age 18 and 6.0% of those age 65 or over.

## Culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Culture")]

St. Charles lies near the eastern end of the [Katy Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Trail_State_Park "Katy Trail State Park"), a 225-mile (362 km) long state park that was adapted from railroad right-of-way. Since the late 1970s, there has been rapid new home construction, commercial and population growth in the St. Charles area. The phrase "Golden Triangle" was coined by developers of this area in the 1980s, referring to the St. Charles County region bordered by highways [Interstate 70](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_70_in_Missouri "Interstate 70 in Missouri"), [Interstate 64](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_64_(Missouri) "Interstate 64 (Missouri)"), and [Route 94](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Route_94 "Missouri Route 94").

St. Charles has a historic shopping district on Main Street. Numerous restored buildings house such tourist destinations as restaurants and various specialty stores. Since 2015, walking food tours on Historic Main Street can be taken through the company Dishing Up America. These tours take customers to the locally famous restaurants in the city.

The city has many special events and features related to the [Lewis and Clark Expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_and_Clark_Expedition "Lewis and Clark Expedition"). In 2007, St. Charles welcomed men's professional [road bicycle racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_bicycle_racing "Road bicycle racing") riders and fans, as it served as the stage 5 final for the [2007 Tour of Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Tour_of_Missouri "2007 Tour of Missouri").

While it does not offer a public golf course, the St. Charles Parks and Recreation System opened a dog park on the north side of the city as a part of DuSable Park-Bales Area in November 2006. This off-leash dog area has two sections – one for smaller dogs, one for larger.

The [St. Charles Convention Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Convention_Center "St. Charles Convention Center") brings visitors, meetings and events to the city. The [Family Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_Arena "Family Arena"), a county-owned 11,000-seat venue, was built in 1999 near the Missouri River. It is used by minor league sports franchises and hosts concerts and events.

### Riverfront

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Riverfront")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/St_Charles_MO_BPOE.JPG/250px-St_Charles_MO_BPOE.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:St_Charles_MO_BPOE.JPG)

Elks Club, 122 S. Main Street

The Riverfront and Main Street area in the [St. Charles Historic District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Historic_District "St. Charles Historic District") is a central gathering place and focal point for the community. The primary features of the riverfront and Historic Main Street are residences and businesses. Each block includes shops, restaurants, and offices. Plans for the development and improvement of the area include a northward extension of the Katy Trail, residential and commercial development, parking garage and casino expansion, and development of hotels.

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/Carolers_St._Charles%2C_Missouri.jpg/250px-Carolers_St._Charles%2C_Missouri.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Carolers_St._Charles,_Missouri.jpg)

Carolers wearing [retro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retro_style "Retro style")[costumes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costume "Costume") sing during the Christmas Traditions Festival

The Christmas Traditions Festival, one of the nation's largest such festivals, takes place annually on the city streets, from the day after Thanksgiving until the Saturday after Christmas. Over 30 costumed Legends of Christmas stroll the streets and interact with guests, and [Victorian Era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_Era "Victorian Era") Christmas Carolers sing old-fashioned carols. Each Saturday and Sunday, the costumed Legends characters and the Lewis & Clark Fife and Drum Corps join the Santa Parade from Historic South Main Street to the site of the [First Missouri State Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Missouri_State_Capitol_State_Historic_Site "First Missouri State Capitol State Historic Site").

On the [Fourth of July](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_of_July "Fourth of July"), fireworks displays draw large numbers on two nights, [July 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence_Day_(United_States) "Independence Day (United States)") and the night before or after the Fourth. The festival, named Riverfest, has been sponsored by the city of St. Charles and organized by a volunteer committee of local leaders.

The Festival of the Little Hills is a historic St. Charles tradition that takes place every year in August, the third full weekend of the month. Started in 1971,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-20) it includes food, live entertainment, craft sales, and shows for kids. The festival is related to the Lewis & Clark expedition, with some participants wearing clothing from the era and re-enacting historic events. Individuals are encouraged to bring homemade items to sell at the festival.

Oktoberfest, held near the river, celebrates the historic German influence on the city, with vendors selling beer and other German goods. It includes a parade. Missouri Tartan Day is a celebration of Scottish American heritage and culture held each spring, coinciding as closely as possible with April 6. This is the anniversary of the signing of the [Declaration of Arbroath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_Arbroath "Declaration of Arbroath") in 1320. The event features a parade with marching bagpipers from around the world and region, Scottish heavy athletics (caber toss, hammer throw, etc.), musical entertainment, traditional and contemporary foods. Highlights include the Kirkin' o' the Tartans (ceremony of blessing for the Scottish clans), displays of traditional Scottish clan tartans, and demonstrations of traditional Scottish activities and games.

The Fete de Glace is an ice-carving competition and demonstration held on North Main Street in mid-January. The Missouri River Irish Festival is held every September in Frontier Park and on Main Street to celebrate Irish Heritage with music, dancing, storytelling, athletics, food, and other entertainment.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-21) During Quilts on Main Street, hundreds of quilts are displayed outside the shops on storefronts and balconies. This event is held annually in September. The Bluegrass Festival in Frontier Park on the big stage of Jaycee's pavilion is held early in September, featuring local and regional acts. The MOSAICS Fine Art Festival is also held on Historic Main Street each September to showcase local, regional and national artists. LGBTQ+ organization Pride St. Charles holds an annual pride festival in June at the St. Charles Family Arena.

## Government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Government")]

See also: [List of mayors of St. Charles, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_St._Charles,_Missouri "List of mayors of St. Charles, Missouri")

St. Charles is a [charter city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charter_city "Charter city") under the [Missouri Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Constitution "Missouri Constitution"), with a City Council as the governing body. One member is elected for each of the ten wards, in an arrangement known as [single-member districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-member_districts "Single-member districts"), and each serves a three-year term.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-25)

The executive head of the city government is the mayor for all legal and ceremonial purposes. Elected at-large for a four-year term, the mayor appoints the members of the various boards, commissions, and committees created by ordinance. The current mayor is Dan Borgmeyer; he was sworn into office on May 7, 2019.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-26)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Education")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/LwdButlerLibrary.jpg/250px-LwdButlerLibrary.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LwdButlerLibrary.jpg)

Butler Library at [Lindenwood University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindenwood_University "Lindenwood University")

The majority of St. Charles is in the [City of St. Charles School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_St._Charles_School_District "City of St. Charles School District").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-CensusSDMap2020-29) That district has six elementary schools, two middle schools, two high schools, and the Lewis & Clark Career Center located at 2400 Zumbehl Road. [St. Charles High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_High_School_(Missouri) "St. Charles High School (Missouri)") (sometimes called SCHS or simply "High") was the first built (1895) of the two high schools. It first operated as a private military academy for boys. In the 1950s, it was acquired by the city and adapted as a public high school. [St. Charles West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_West_High_School "St. Charles West High School") (SCW or simply West) was constructed in the late 1970s in response to the city's growing population. St. Charles West had its first graduation in 1979. St. Charles High School underwent renovation in 1995 to improve both the exterior and interior of the building. St. Charles West was renovated in 2005, and a new library and auxiliary gym were built. The city is also served by Jefferson Intermediate, which has all 5th and 6th grade classes, and Hardin Middle School, which has all 7th and 8th grade classes.

Some parts of St. Charles are in other school districts: southern portions are in the [Francis Howell School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Howell_School_District "Francis Howell School District"), while northern parts are in the [Orchard Farm School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orchard_Farm_School_District "Orchard Farm School District").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-CensusSDMap2020-29) Many students who live on the southern edge of St. Charles City attend Henderson, Becky David, or Harvest Ridge elementary schools, Barnwell Middle, and [Francis Howell North High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Howell_North_High_School "Francis Howell North High School"). To the North, the Orchard Farm School District also serves St. Charles. Like the Francis Howell School District, its administrative offices are not in St. Charles, and it has two elementary schools, a middle school, and a high school.

A variety of private schools also operate here, each affiliated with a religious denomination. These include Immanuel Lutheran (Pre-K to 8), Zion Lutheran (Pre-K to 8), St. Charles Borromeo, St. Peter's, St. Cletus (K–8), Academy of the Sacred Heart (founded by [Saint Rose Philippine Duchesne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Rose_Philippine_Duchesne "Saint Rose Philippine Duchesne"), and the site of her shrine), [Duchesne High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duchesne_High_School_(Missouri) "Duchesne High School (Missouri)") (formerly named St. Peter High school), and St. Elizabeth Ann Seton-St. Robert Bellarmine (K–8).

[Lindenwood University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindenwood_University "Lindenwood University") is located on Kingshighway, near downtown St. Charles and St. Charles High. Founded by Major George Sibley and his wife Mary in 1827 as a women's school named Lindenwood School for Girls, the institution is the second-oldest higher-education institution west of the Mississippi River.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-30) The private university is affiliated with the Presbyterian Church.

In the 21st century, LU is one of the fastest-growing universities in the Midwest. It enrolls close to 15,000 students. In 2006, it briefly attracted publicity when [People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_for_the_Ethical_Treatment_of_Animals "People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals") staged a small protest against its unusual tuition fee policies: In an effort to help rural students pay for higher education, LU allowed families to sell livestock to the school. The animals were slaughtered and processed for serving at campus dining halls.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-31) Lindenwood hosts 89.1 The Wood ([KCLC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KCLC "KCLC")), a commercial-free student-driven radio station.

St. Charles was also home to the now defunct [St. Charles College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_College_(Missouri) "St. Charles College (Missouri)") (not to be confused with [St. Charles Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Community_College "St. Charles Community College")),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-32) and [Vatterott College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatterott_College "Vatterott College").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-33)

According to the [Federal Highway Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Highway_Administration "Federal Highway Administration"), St. Charles was the site of the first interstate highway project in the nation.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-34) Major highways include [Interstate 70](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_70_in_Missouri "Interstate 70 in Missouri"), Missouri 370, Missouri 94, and Missouri 364. Also see: [St. Charles Area Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Area_Transit "St. Charles Area Transit")

The "St. Charles City Streetcar" was a proposed new [heritage streetcar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heritage_streetcar "Heritage streetcar") line to be built connecting the New Town, Missouri residential development to the heart of the city of [St. Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Charles,_Missouri "Saint Charles, Missouri").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-newtown-35) It was a joint effort between Whittaker Builders, Inc, and the City of St. Charles and [St. Charles Area Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Area_Transit "St. Charles Area Transit").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-TrolleyCarsArrive-36) A minimum of nine vintage [PCC streetcars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCC_streetcar "PCC streetcar") (not to be confused with [cable cars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cable_car_(railway) "Cable car (railway)")), had been purchased from the [San Francisco area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F_Market_&_Wharves "F Market & Wharves") by Whittaker Builders for use and spare parts.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-TrolleyCarsArrive-36) The project stalled, and in 2012, the streetcars purchased by Whittaker Builders were scrapped following a fire. Whittaker, a developer of the New Town project and principal partner with the city on the streetcar project, has since gone bankrupt,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-37) ending the proposed street car line.

**Saint Charles** (commonly abbreviated **St. Charles**) is a city in and the [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") of [St. Charles County, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri "St. Charles County, Missouri"), United States.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-GR6-2) The population was 70,493 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), making St. Charles the [eighth-most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Missouri "List of cities in Missouri") in [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"). Situated on the [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River") near its mouth at the [Mississippi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_River "Mississippi River"), St. Charles is approximately 20 miles northwest of St. Louis.

The city was founded circa 1769 as Les Petites Côtes, or "The Little Hillsides" in French, by [Louis Blanchette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Blanchette "Louis Blanchette"), a French-Canadian fur trader.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-3) The St. Charles area was settled primarily by French-speaking colonists from Canada in its early days. This former [French territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Country "Illinois Country") west of the Mississippi River was nominally ruled [by Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Louisiana "Spanish Louisiana") following France's defeat in the [Seven Years' War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Years'_War "Seven Years' War"), while France had also ceded the east of the Mississippi to Great Britain. St. Charles is thus the third-oldest city in what is now the state of [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"). In the 18th and 19th century, the city's waterfront played a significant role as a river port for westward trade and expansion, including trade with Native American tribes on the upper Missouri River.

In 1804, the [Lewis and Clark Expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_and_Clark_Expedition "Lewis and Clark Expedition") considered this settlement the last "civilized" stop before they headed upriver to explore the western territory that the United States acquired from France in the [Louisiana Purchase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Purchase "Louisiana Purchase").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-4)

The city served as the first Missouri capital from 1821 to 1826.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-5) It was also the starting point of the [Boone's Lick Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boone's_Lick_Road "Boone's Lick Road") to the [Boonslick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boonslick "Boonslick") and the [Santa Fe Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Trail "Santa Fe Trail"). In the 20th century, it became the site of the [Saint Rose Philippine Duchesne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Rose_Philippine_Duchesne "Saint Rose Philippine Duchesne") Catholic shrine.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-6)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

[Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") peoples inhabited the area at least as early as 11,000 B.C. When European colonists arrived, the area was inhabited by the historic Ilini, Osage and Missouri tribes.

According to Hopewell's _Legends of the Missouri and Mississippi_, Blanchette met another French Canadian (Bernard Guillet) at this site in 1765. Blanchette, determined to settle there, asked if Guillet, who had become an honorary chief of a [Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lakota_people "Lakota people") band, had chosen a name for it.

"I called the place 'Les Petites Côtes' " replied Bernard, "from the sides of the hills that you see.""By that name shall it be called", said Blanchette Chasseur, "for it is the echo of nature—beautiful from its simplicity."
Blanchette settled there _circa_ 1769 under the authority of the Spanish governor of [Upper Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Louisiana "Upper Louisiana") (the area had been ceded by France [to Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Louisiana "Spanish Louisiana") under an agreement with Great Britain following French defeat in the [French and Indian Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_and_Indian_Wars "French and Indian Wars")). He was appointed as the territory's civil and military leader, serving until his death in 1793. Although the settlement was under Spanish jurisdiction, the settlers were primarily Native American and French Canadians who had migrated from northern territories and most of whom spoke French.

Considered to begin in St. Charles, the [Boone's Lick Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boone's_Lick_Road "Boone's Lick Road") along the Missouri River was the major overland route for European-American settlement of central and western Missouri. This area became known as the [Boonslick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boonslick "Boonslick") or "Boonslick Country." At [Franklin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin,_Missouri "Franklin, Missouri"), the trail ended.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-7) Westward progress continued on the [Santa Fe Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Fe_Trail "Santa Fe Trail").

### San Carlos Borromeo

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: San Carlos Borromeo")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Sacred_Heart_Convent_and_Saint_Charles_Borromeo_Catholic_Church_in_Saint_Charles.jpg/330px-Sacred_Heart_Convent_and_Saint_Charles_Borromeo_Catholic_Church_in_Saint_Charles.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sacred_Heart_Convent_and_Saint_Charles_Borromeo_Catholic_Church_in_Saint_Charles.jpg)

Sacred Heart Convent and Saint Charles Borromeo Catholic Church, 1908

The first church, built in 1791, was Catholic and dedicated to the Italian saint [Charles Borromeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Borromeo "Charles Borromeo"), under the Spanish version of his name, San Carlos Borromeo. The town became known as San Carlos del Misuri (St. Charles of the Missouri). The original location of the church is not known but a replica has been built just off Main Street. The fourth St. Charles Borromeo Church now stands on Fifth Street.

The Spanish Lieutenant-Governor [Carlos de Hault de Lassus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_de_Hault_de_Lassus "Carlos de Hault de Lassus") appointed [Daniel Boone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Boone "Daniel Boone") as commandant of the [Femme Osage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femme_Osage?action=edit&redlink=1 "Femme Osage (page does not exist)") District. He served in this role until the United States government acquired control in 1804 following the [Louisiana Purchase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisiana_Purchase "Louisiana Purchase") from France.

The name of the town, San Carlos, was anglicized to St. Charles. [William Clark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Clark_(explorer) "William Clark (explorer)") arrived in St. Charles on May 16, 1804. With him were 40 men and three boats; they made final preparations for their major cross-country expedition, as they waited for [Meriwether Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meriwether_Lewis "Meriwether Lewis") to arrive from St. Louis. They attended dances, dinners, and a church service during this time. Excited to be part of the national expedition, the townspeople were very hospitable to the explorers. Lewis arrived via [St. Charles Rock Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Rock_Road "St. Charles Rock Road") on May 20. The expedition launched the next day in a [keel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keel "Keel") boat at 3:30 pm. St. Charles was the last established European-American town that the expedition visited for more than two and a half years.

### State capital and growth

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: State capital and growth")]

When Missouri was granted statehood in 1821, the legislature decided to build a "City of [Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Jefferson "Thomas Jefferson")" to serve as the state capital, in the center of the state, overlooking the Missouri River. Since this land was undeveloped at the time, a temporary capital was needed. St. Charles was chosen over eight other cities in a competition to house the temporary capital. It offered free meeting space for the legislature in rooms located above a hardware store. This building is preserved as the [First Missouri State Capitol State Historic Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Missouri_State_Capitol_State_Historic_Site "First Missouri State Capitol State Historic Site") and may be toured. The Missouri government continued to meet there until buildings were completed in [Jefferson City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jefferson_City,_Missouri "Jefferson City, Missouri") in 1826.

[Gottfried Duden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gottfried_Duden "Gottfried Duden") was a German who visited in the area in 1824. Travelling under the guidance of Daniel M. Boone, he wrote extensive accounts of life in [St. Charles County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri "St. Charles County, Missouri") during his year there. He published these after returning to Germany in 1829, and his favorable impressions of the area led to the immigration of a number of Germans in 1833. The first permanent German settler in the region was probably Louis Eversman, who had arrived with Duden but decided to stay.

In the post-World War II era, the federal government undertook a major program of interstate highway construction. St. Charles is where the first claimed interstate project was started in 1956. A state highway marker is displayed with a logo and information regarding this claim, off Interstate 70 going westbound, to the right of the First Capitol Drive exit.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Kansas and Pennsylvania also claim to have had the first interstate project.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-8)

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Climate")]

St. Charles has a Köppen humid subtropical climate, with warm and humid summers (eventual hot days) and cool winters (with short cold spells possible sometimes). Precipitation is mostly light to moderate, with occasional stormy weather. Spring is the wettest season on average.

## Culture

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Culture")]

St. Charles lies near the eastern end of the [Katy Trail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Trail_State_Park "Katy Trail State Park"), a 225-mile (362 km) long state park that was adapted from railroad right-of-way. Since the late 1970s, there has been rapid new home construction, commercial and population growth in the St. Charles area. The phrase "Golden Triangle" was coined by developers of this area in the 1980s, referring to the St. Charles County region bordered by highways [Interstate 70](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_70_in_Missouri "Interstate 70 in Missouri"), [Interstate 64](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_64_(Missouri) "Interstate 64 (Missouri)"), and [Route 94](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Route_94 "Missouri Route 94").

St. Charles has a historic shopping district on Main Street. Numerous restored buildings house such tourist destinations as restaurants and various specialty stores. Since 2015, walking food tours on Historic Main Street can be taken through the company Dishing Up America. These tours take customers to the locally famous restaurants in the city.

The city has many special events and features related to the [Lewis and Clark Expedition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_and_Clark_Expedition "Lewis and Clark Expedition"). In 2007, St. Charles welcomed men's professional [road bicycle racing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_bicycle_racing "Road bicycle racing") riders and fans, as it served as the stage 5 final for the [2007 Tour of Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_Tour_of_Missouri "2007 Tour of Missouri").

While it does not offer a public golf course, the St. Charles Parks and Recreation System opened a dog park on the north side of the city as a part of DuSable Park-Bales Area in November 2006. This off-leash dog area has two sections – one for smaller dogs, one for larger.

The [St. Charles Convention Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Convention_Center "St. Charles Convention Center") brings visitors, meetings and events to the city. The [Family Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_Arena "Family Arena"), a county-owned 11,000-seat venue, was built in 1999 near the Missouri River. It is used by minor league sports franchises and hosts concerts and events.

### Riverfront

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Riverfront")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/57/St_Charles_MO_BPOE.JPG/250px-St_Charles_MO_BPOE.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:St_Charles_MO_BPOE.JPG)

Elks Club, 122 S. Main Street

The Riverfront and Main Street area in the [St. Charles Historic District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Historic_District "St. Charles Historic District") is a central gathering place and focal point for the community. The primary features of the riverfront and Historic Main Street are residences and businesses. Each block includes shops, restaurants, and offices. Plans for the development and improvement of the area include a northward extension of the Katy Trail, residential and commercial development, parking garage and casino expansion, and development of hotels.

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/03/Carolers_St._Charles%2C_Missouri.jpg/250px-Carolers_St._Charles%2C_Missouri.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Carolers_St._Charles,_Missouri.jpg)

Carolers wearing [retro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retro_style "Retro style")[costumes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costume "Costume") sing during the Christmas Traditions Festival

The Christmas Traditions Festival, one of the nation's largest such festivals, takes place annually on the city streets, from the day after Thanksgiving until the Saturday after Christmas. Over 30 costumed Legends of Christmas stroll the streets and interact with guests, and [Victorian Era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victorian_Era "Victorian Era") Christmas Carolers sing old-fashioned carols. Each Saturday and Sunday, the costumed Legends characters and the Lewis & Clark Fife and Drum Corps join the Santa Parade from Historic South Main Street to the site of the [First Missouri State Capitol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Missouri_State_Capitol_State_Historic_Site "First Missouri State Capitol State Historic Site").

On the [Fourth of July](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_of_July "Fourth of July"), fireworks displays draw large numbers on two nights, [July 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independence_Day_(United_States) "Independence Day (United States)") and the night before or after the Fourth. The festival, named Riverfest, has been sponsored by the city of St. Charles and organized by a volunteer committee of local leaders.

The Festival of the Little Hills is a historic St. Charles tradition that takes place every year in August, the third full weekend of the month. Started in 1971,[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-20) it includes food, live entertainment, craft sales, and shows for kids. The festival is related to the Lewis & Clark expedition, with some participants wearing clothing from the era and re-enacting historic events. Individuals are encouraged to bring homemade items to sell at the festival.

Oktoberfest, held near the river, celebrates the historic German influence on the city, with vendors selling beer and other German goods. It includes a parade. Missouri Tartan Day is a celebration of Scottish American heritage and culture held each spring, coinciding as closely as possible with April 6. This is the anniversary of the signing of the [Declaration of Arbroath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Declaration_of_Arbroath "Declaration of Arbroath") in 1320. The event features a parade with marching bagpipers from around the world and region, Scottish heavy athletics (caber toss, hammer throw, etc.), musical entertainment, traditional and contemporary foods. Highlights include the Kirkin' o' the Tartans (ceremony of blessing for the Scottish clans), displays of traditional Scottish clan tartans, and demonstrations of traditional Scottish activities and games.

The Fete de Glace is an ice-carving competition and demonstration held on North Main Street in mid-January. The Missouri River Irish Festival is held every September in Frontier Park and on Main Street to celebrate Irish Heritage with music, dancing, storytelling, athletics, food, and other entertainment.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-21) During Quilts on Main Street, hundreds of quilts are displayed outside the shops on storefronts and balconies. This event is held annually in September. The Bluegrass Festival in Frontier Park on the big stage of Jaycee's pavilion is held early in September, featuring local and regional acts. The MOSAICS Fine Art Festival is also held on Historic Main Street each September to showcase local, regional and national artists. LGBTQ+ organization Pride St. Charles holds an annual pride festival in June at the St. Charles Family Arena.

## Government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Government")]

See also: [List of mayors of St. Charles, Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_St._Charles,_Missouri "List of mayors of St. Charles, Missouri")

St. Charles is a [charter city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charter_city "Charter city") under the [Missouri Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Constitution "Missouri Constitution"), with a City Council as the governing body. One member is elected for each of the ten wards, in an arrangement known as [single-member districts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-member_districts "Single-member districts"), and each serves a three-year term.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-25)

The executive head of the city government is the mayor for all legal and ceremonial purposes. Elected at-large for a four-year term, the mayor appoints the members of the various boards, commissions, and committees created by ordinance. The current mayor is Dan Borgmeyer; he was sworn into office on May 7, 2019.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-26)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles,_Missouri&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Education")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/25/LwdButlerLibrary.jpg/250px-LwdButlerLibrary.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LwdButlerLibrary.jpg)

Butler Library at [Lindenwood University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindenwood_University "Lindenwood University")

The majority of St. Charles is in the [City of St. Charles School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City_of_St._Charles_School_District "City of St. Charles School District").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-CensusSDMap2020-29) That district has six elementary schools, two middle schools, two high schools, and the Lewis & Clark Career Center located at 2400 Zumbehl Road. [St. Charles High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_High_School_(Missouri) "St. Charles High School (Missouri)") (sometimes called SCHS or simply "High") was the first built (1895) of the two high schools. It first operated as a private military academy for boys. In the 1950s, it was acquired by the city and adapted as a public high school. [St. Charles West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_West_High_School "St. Charles West High School") (SCW or simply West) was constructed in the late 1970s in response to the city's growing population. St. Charles West had its first graduation in 1979. St. Charles High School underwent renovation in 1995 to improve both the exterior and interior of the building. St. Charles West was renovated in 2005, and a new library and auxiliary gym were built. The city is also served by Jefferson Intermediate, which has all 5th and 6th grade classes, and Hardin Middle School, which has all 7th and 8th grade classes.

Some parts of St. Charles are in other school districts: southern portions are in the [Francis Howell School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Howell_School_District "Francis Howell School District"), while northern parts are in the [Orchard Farm School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orchard_Farm_School_District "Orchard Farm School District").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-CensusSDMap2020-29) Many students who live on the southern edge of St. Charles City attend Henderson, Becky David, or Harvest Ridge elementary schools, Barnwell Middle, and [Francis Howell North High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Howell_North_High_School "Francis Howell North High School"). To the North, the Orchard Farm School District also serves St. Charles. Like the Francis Howell School District, its administrative offices are not in St. Charles, and it has two elementary schools, a middle school, and a high school.

A variety of private schools also operate here, each affiliated with a religious denomination. These include Immanuel Lutheran (Pre-K to 8), Zion Lutheran (Pre-K to 8), St. Charles Borromeo, St. Peter's, St. Cletus (K–8), Academy of the Sacred Heart (founded by [Saint Rose Philippine Duchesne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Rose_Philippine_Duchesne "Saint Rose Philippine Duchesne"), and the site of her shrine), [Duchesne High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duchesne_High_School_(Missouri) "Duchesne High School (Missouri)") (formerly named St. Peter High school), and St. Elizabeth Ann Seton-St. Robert Bellarmine (K–8).

[Lindenwood University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindenwood_University "Lindenwood University") is located on Kingshighway, near downtown St. Charles and St. Charles High. Founded by Major George Sibley and his wife Mary in 1827 as a women's school named Lindenwood School for Girls, the institution is the second-oldest higher-education institution west of the Mississippi River.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-30) The private university is affiliated with the Presbyterian Church.

In the 21st century, LU is one of the fastest-growing universities in the Midwest. It enrolls close to 15,000 students. In 2006, it briefly attracted publicity when [People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People_for_the_Ethical_Treatment_of_Animals "People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals") staged a small protest against its unusual tuition fee policies: In an effort to help rural students pay for higher education, LU allowed families to sell livestock to the school. The animals were slaughtered and processed for serving at campus dining halls.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-31) Lindenwood hosts 89.1 The Wood ([KCLC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KCLC "KCLC")), a commercial-free student-driven radio station.

St. Charles was also home to the now defunct [St. Charles College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_College_(Missouri) "St. Charles College (Missouri)") (not to be confused with [St. Charles Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Community_College "St. Charles Community College")),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-32) and [Vatterott College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatterott_College "Vatterott College").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-33)

The "St. Charles City Streetcar" was a proposed new [heritage streetcar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heritage_streetcar "Heritage streetcar") line to be built connecting the New Town, Missouri residential development to the heart of the city of [St. Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Charles,_Missouri "Saint Charles, Missouri").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-newtown-35) It was a joint effort between Whittaker Builders, Inc, and the City of St. Charles and [St. Charles Area Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Area_Transit "St. Charles Area Transit").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-TrolleyCarsArrive-36) A minimum of nine vintage [PCC streetcars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCC_streetcar "PCC streetcar") (not to be confused with [cable cars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cable_car_(railway) "Cable car (railway)")), had been purchased from the [San Francisco area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/F_Market_&_Wharves "F Market & Wharves") by Whittaker Builders for use and spare parts.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-TrolleyCarsArrive-36) The project stalled, and in 2012, the streetcars purchased by Whittaker Builders were scrapped following a fire. Whittaker, a developer of the New Town project and principal partner with the city on the streetcar project, has since gone bankrupt,[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles,_Missouri#cite_note-37) ending the proposed street car line.

**St. Charles County** is located in the central eastern part of the [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"). As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_Census "2020 United States Census"), the population was 405,262,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-QF-1) making it Missouri's third-most populous [county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_(United_States) "County (United States)"). Its [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") is St. Charles.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-GR6-2) The county was organized October 1, 1812, and named for Saint [Charles Borromeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Borromeo "Charles Borromeo"), an Italian cardinal.

St. Charles County is part of the [St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis "St. Louis"), MO-[IL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois")[Metropolitan Statistical Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_St._Louis "Greater St. Louis") and contains many of the city's northwestern [suburbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suburb "Suburb"). The wealthiest county in [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-3) St. Charles County is one of the nation's fastest-growing counties.

St. Charles County includes a part of the [Augusta AVA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augusta_AVA "Augusta AVA"), an area of vineyards and wineries designated by the federal government in 1980 as the first [American Viticultural Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Viticultural_Area "American Viticultural Area").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-Pingelton-4) The county's rural outer edge along the south-facing bluffs above the [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River"), is also part of the broader [Missouri Rhineland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Rhineland "Missouri Rhineland").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The County of St. Charles was originally called the District of St. Charles and had no definite limits until 1816 to 1818 when neighboring counties were formed.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-5) The borders of St. Charles are the same today as they were in 1818.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-6)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9d/Boltonia_decurrens_millar.jpg/250px-Boltonia_decurrens_millar.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Boltonia_decurrens_millar.jpg)

St. Charles County is the only known habitat of the threatened decurrent false aster in Missouri.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-7)

According to the [U.S. Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Census_Bureau "U.S. Census Bureau"), the county has a total area of 593 square miles (1,540 km 2), of which 560 square miles (1,500 km 2) is land and 32 square miles (83 km 2) (5.4%) is water.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-GR1-8)

The highest elevation is 901 feet (275 m) northwest of Augusta near Femme Osage Creek headwaters.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-9)

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the county had a population of 405,262, a median age of 39.3 years, 23.4% of residents under the age of 18, and 16.1% of residents 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 95.6 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 93.3 males.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DP-17) The population density was 643 inhabitants per square mile (248/km 2).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-18)

The racial makeup of the county was 83.8% White, 5.2% Black or African American, 0.2% American Indian and Alaska Native, 2.8% Asian, 0.1% Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander, 1.5% from some other race, and 6.5% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino residents of any race comprised 4.0% of the population.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020PL-19)

94.3% of residents lived in urban areas, while 5.7% lived in rural areas.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DHC-20)

There were 154,851 households in the county, of which 32.8% had children under the age of 18 living with them and 22.9% had a female householder with no spouse or partner present. About 23.7% of all households were made up of individuals and 9.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DP-17)

There were 161,144 housing units, of which 3.9% were vacant. Among occupied housing units, 78.8% were owner-occupied and 21.2% were renter-occupied. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.8% and the rental vacancy rate was 7.1%.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DP-17)

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

There were 101,663 households, out of which 40.50% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 63.20% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 9.20% have a woman whose husband does not live with her, and 24.20% were non-families. 19.40% of all households were made up of individuals, and 5.90% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.76 and the average family size was 3.18.

In the county, the population was spread out in age, with 29.00% under the age of 18, 8.20% from 18 to 24, 32.60% from 25 to 44, 21.60% from 45 to 64, and 8.80% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 34 years. For every 100 females there were 97.10 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 94.10 males.

The median income for a household in the county was $71,458, and the median income for a family was $64,415. Males had a median income of $44,528 versus $29,405 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the county was $23,592. 4.00% of the population and 2.80% of families were below the poverty line. Out of the total people living in poverty, 4.90% are under the age of 18 and 5.10% are 65 or older.

St. Charles County has had one of the fastest-growing populations in the state for many decades, with 55% growth in the 1970s, 48% in the 1980s, 33% in the 1990s, and another 27% in the 2000s. The county sits at a cross-section of industry, as well as extensive retail and some agriculture. With the [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River") on the south and east and the [Mississippi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_River "Mississippi River") on the north, the county is bisected east to west by Interstate 70. After [St. Charles Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Airport "St. Charles Airport") closed in 2010, the county has one remaining small airport, [St. Charles County Smartt Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County_Smartt_Airport "St. Charles County Smartt Airport"). Two ferries cross the Mississippi River from St. Charles County.

## Government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Government")]

St. Charles County is governed by a county executive and a county council. The county council consists of seven members, each elected from various districts in the county. The county executive is elected by the entire county. The current executive is Steve Ehlmann. He was preceded by Joe Ortwerth, who was preceded by Gene Schwendemann, the first county executive of St. Charles County under the new form of government. The executive under the old form of county government was termed a "judge." The county had 258,525 registered voters as of March 2016.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-32)

St. Charles County Ambulance District (SCCAD) is the largest such district in Missouri, serving all of St. Charles County and its population of nearly 370,000.

### Law enforcement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Law enforcement")]

The St. Charles County Sheriff's Department (SCCSD) is responsible for court services and security, prisoner transport, [civil process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_of_process "Service of process"), and [bailiffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bailiff "Bailiff"). Until the end of 2014, SCCSD was the primary law enforcement agency serving unincorporated areas of St. Charles County. On January 1, 2015, the St. Charles County Police Department was established and assumed that responsibility.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-33) It should not be confused with the [St. Charles City Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_City_Police_Department "St. Charles City Police Department"). The St. Charles County Regional [SWAT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SWAT "SWAT") Team is made up of officers from each county law enforcement agency.

The SCCPD Aviation Unit is part of a multi-jurisdictional unit known as the Metro Air Support Unit, with the [Metropolitan Police Department, City of St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Police_Department,_City_of_St._Louis "Metropolitan Police Department, City of St. Louis"); [St. Louis County Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_County_Police_Department "St. Louis County Police Department"); and St. Charles County Police Department.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-34) As of 2024, the fleet included five helicopters,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-35) and twelve pilots or pilots in training.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In May 2022, Ryan Keuhner, who was then an SCCSD deputy, shot and killed his neighbor's 3-year-old rescue dog with a [pellet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pellet_(air_gun) "Pellet (air gun)") gun. The shooting was reportedly unprovoked and Keuhner was off duty at the time. Video of the dog's owner confronting Keuhner was uploaded online, and later gained national coverage. Keuhner resigned in June 2022 and was charged with a class A [misdemeanor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misdemeanor "Misdemeanor") for animal abuse.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-37)

### Library resolution

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Library resolution")]

In 2023, the county council issued a resolution aimed at library policies and staff online activities. The resolution followed protests and comments at council meetings from residents who complained about a staff member wearing [gender non-conforming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender_non-conforming "Gender non-conforming") clothes. Within the resolution, the council asked the library CEO to remove an article they shared on their personal [LinkedIn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LinkedIn "LinkedIn") profile related to conservative campaigns targeting public libraries and [freedom of speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_of_speech "Freedom of speech").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-38)

### Federal politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Federal politics")]

St. Charles County has long been a Republican stronghold despite being an urban county, likely due to being the wealthiest county in Missouri.

Despite this, it did vote for [Medicaid expansion in 2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Missouri_Amendment_2 "2020 Missouri Amendment 2"), [legal recreational marijuana in 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Missouri_Amendment_3 "2022 Missouri Amendment 3"), and [legal abortion in 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Missouri_Amendment_3 "2024 Missouri Amendment 3"). It was also one of the few counties in Missouri to shift towards the Democrats from 2020 to 2024.

#### 2016 Missouri presidential primary results

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: 2016 Missouri presidential primary results")]

**Republican**

[Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") won the most votes in St. Charles County, with 41.50 percent. U.S. Senator [Ted Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Cruz "Ted Cruz") (R-[Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas")) came in second with 38.87 percent, Governor [John Kasich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kasich "John Kasich") (R-[Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio "Ohio")) placed third with 10.70 percent, and U.S. Senator [Marco Rubio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Rubio "Marco Rubio") (R-[Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida")) was fourth with 7.10 percent.

**Democratic**

U.S. Senator [Bernie Sanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernie_Sanders "Bernie Sanders") (I-[Vermont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vermont "Vermont")) won the primary with 54.32 percent to former [Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State")[Hillary Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton")'s 44.80 percent.

#### 2012 Missouri presidential primary results

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: 2012 Missouri presidential primary results")]

**Republican**

Former U.S. Senator [Rick Santorum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Santorum "Rick Santorum") (R-[Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania")) won the most votes in St. Charles County, with 56.29 percent. Former Governor [Mitt Romney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney "Mitt Romney") (R-[Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts")) came in second with 25.43 percent, and former U.S. Representative [Ron Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Paul "Ron Paul") (R-[Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas")) was third with 12.69 percent.

**Democratic**

With incumbent President [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") facing no serious opposition, few St. Charles County voters voted in the Democratic primary; Obama won 87.83 percent.

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: 2008 Missouri presidential primary results")]

**Republican**

Former Governor [Mitt Romney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney "Mitt Romney") (R-[Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massachusetts "Massachusetts")) won the most votes in St. Charles County, with 37.72 percent. U.S. Senator [John McCain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McCain "John McCain") (R-[Arizona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona "Arizona")) came in second with 34.95 percent, former Governor [Mike Huckabee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Huckabee "Mike Huckabee") (R-[Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas "Arkansas")) placed third with 21.83 percent, and U.S. Representative [Ron Paul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Paul "Ron Paul") (R-[Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas")) was fourth with 3.83 percent.

### Westplex

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=35 "Edit section: Westplex")]

Westplex is an area within [St. Charles County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County "St. Charles County") in east-central [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri") to the west of [St. Louis County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_County,_Missouri "St. Louis County, Missouri").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-westplexcom-51)

The Westplex is part of St. Charles County that used to be called "The Golden Triangle". The "triangle" was formed by I-70 to the north, Missouri Route 94 to the southeast, and I-64 to the southwest. Since almost all of the growth in St. Charles County was within this triangle it was dubbed the "Golden" area of St. Charles County, hence, Golden Triangle. Today the Westplex is made up of St. Charles, [St. Peters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peters,_Missouri "St. Peters, Missouri"), [Weldon Spring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weldon_Spring,_Missouri "Weldon Spring, Missouri"), [Cottleville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cottleville,_Missouri "Cottleville, Missouri"), [Dardenne Prairie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dardenne_Prairie,_Missouri "Dardenne Prairie, Missouri"), [O'Fallon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/O'Fallon,_Missouri "O'Fallon, Missouri"), [Lake St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_St._Louis,_Missouri "Lake St. Louis, Missouri"), and [Wentzville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wentzville,_Missouri "Wentzville, Missouri").

**St. Charles County** is located in the central eastern part of the [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"). As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_Census "2020 United States Census"), the population was 405,262,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-QF-1) making it Missouri's third-most populous [county](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_(United_States) "County (United States)"). Its [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat") is St. Charles.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-GR6-2) The county was organized October 1, 1812, and named for Saint [Charles Borromeo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Borromeo "Charles Borromeo"), an Italian cardinal.

St. Charles County is part of the [St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis "St. Louis"), MO-[IL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois")[Metropolitan Statistical Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_St._Louis "Greater St. Louis") and contains many of the city's northwestern [suburbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suburb "Suburb"). The wealthiest county in [Missouri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri "Missouri"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-3) St. Charles County is one of the nation's fastest-growing counties.

St. Charles County includes a part of the [Augusta AVA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Augusta_AVA "Augusta AVA"), an area of vineyards and wineries designated by the federal government in 1980 as the first [American Viticultural Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Viticultural_Area "American Viticultural Area").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-Pingelton-4) The county's rural outer edge along the south-facing bluffs above the [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River"), is also part of the broader [Missouri Rhineland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_Rhineland "Missouri Rhineland").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The County of St. Charles was originally called the District of St. Charles and had no definite limits until 1816 to 1818 when neighboring counties were formed.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-5) The borders of St. Charles are the same today as they were in 1818.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-6)

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

St. Charles County is the only known habitat of the threatened decurrent false aster in Missouri.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-7)

According to the [U.S. Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Census_Bureau "U.S. Census Bureau"), the county has a total area of 593 square miles (1,540 km 2), of which 560 square miles (1,500 km 2) is land and 32 square miles (83 km 2) (5.4%) is water.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-GR1-8)

The highest elevation is 901 feet (275 m) northwest of Augusta near Femme Osage Creek headwaters.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-9)

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the county had a population of 405,262, a median age of 39.3 years, 23.4% of residents under the age of 18, and 16.1% of residents 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females there were 95.6 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and over there were 93.3 males.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DP-17) The population density was 643 inhabitants per square mile (248/km 2).[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-18)

The racial makeup of the county was 83.8% White, 5.2% Black or African American, 0.2% American Indian and Alaska Native, 2.8% Asian, 0.1% Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander, 1.5% from some other race, and 6.5% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino residents of any race comprised 4.0% of the population.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020PL-19)

94.3% of residents lived in urban areas, while 5.7% lived in rural areas.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DHC-20)

There were 154,851 households in the county, of which 32.8% had children under the age of 18 living with them and 22.9% had a female householder with no spouse or partner present. About 23.7% of all households were made up of individuals and 9.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DP-17)

There were 161,144 housing units, of which 3.9% were vacant. Among occupied housing units, 78.8% were owner-occupied and 21.2% were renter-occupied. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.8% and the rental vacancy rate was 7.1%.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-Census2020DP-17)

### 2000 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: 2000 census")]

There were 101,663 households, out of which 40.50% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 63.20% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 9.20% have a woman whose husband does not live with her, and 24.20% were non-families. 19.40% of all households were made up of individuals, and 5.90% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.76 and the average family size was 3.18.

In the county, the population was spread out in age, with 29.00% under the age of 18, 8.20% from 18 to 24, 32.60% from 25 to 44, 21.60% from 45 to 64, and 8.80% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 34 years. For every 100 females there were 97.10 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 94.10 males.

The median income for a household in the county was $71,458, and the median income for a family was $64,415. Males had a median income of $44,528 versus $29,405 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for the county was $23,592. 4.00% of the population and 2.80% of families were below the poverty line. Out of the total people living in poverty, 4.90% are under the age of 18 and 5.10% are 65 or older.

St. Charles County has had one of the fastest-growing populations in the state for many decades, with 55% growth in the 1970s, 48% in the 1980s, 33% in the 1990s, and another 27% in the 2000s. The county sits at a cross-section of industry, as well as extensive retail and some agriculture. With the [Missouri River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Missouri_River "Missouri River") on the south and east and the [Mississippi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_River "Mississippi River") on the north, the county is bisected east to west by Interstate 70. After [St. Charles Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Airport "St. Charles Airport") closed in 2010, the county has one remaining small airport, [St. Charles County Smartt Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County_Smartt_Airport "St. Charles County Smartt Airport"). Two ferries cross the Mississippi River from St. Charles County.

## Government

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Government")]

St. Charles County is governed by a county executive and a county council. The county council consists of seven members, each elected from various districts in the county. The county executive is elected by the entire county. The current executive is Steve Ehlmann. He was preceded by Joe Ortwerth, who was preceded by Gene Schwendemann, the first county executive of St. Charles County under the new form of government. The executive under the old form of county government was termed a "judge." The county had 258,525 registered voters as of March 2016.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-32)

St. Charles County Ambulance District (SCCAD) is the largest such district in Missouri, serving all of St. Charles County and its population of nearly 370,000.

### Law enforcement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Law enforcement")]

The St. Charles County Sheriff's Department (SCCSD) is responsible for court services and security, prisoner transport, [civil process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_of_process "Service of process"), and [bailiffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bailiff "Bailiff"). Until the end of 2014, SCCSD was the primary law enforcement agency serving unincorporated areas of St. Charles County. On January 1, 2015, the St. Charles County Police Department was established and assumed that responsibility.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-33) It should not be confused with the [St. Charles City Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_City_Police_Department "St. Charles City Police Department"). The St. Charles County Regional [SWAT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SWAT "SWAT") Team is made up of officers from each county law enforcement agency.

The SCCPD Aviation Unit is part of a multi-jurisdictional unit known as the Metro Air Support Unit, with the [Metropolitan Police Department, City of St. Louis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_Police_Department,_City_of_St._Louis "Metropolitan Police Department, City of St. Louis"); [St. Louis County Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Louis_County_Police_Department "St. Louis County Police Department"); and St. Charles County Police Department.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-34) As of 2024, the fleet included five helicopters,[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-35) and twelve pilots or pilots in training.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In May 2022, Ryan Keuhner, who was then an SCCSD deputy, shot and killed his neighbor's 3-year-old rescue dog with a [pellet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pellet_(air_gun) "Pellet (air gun)") gun. The shooting was reportedly unprovoked and Keuhner was off duty at the time. Video of the dog's owner confronting Keuhner was uploaded online, and later gained national coverage. Keuhner resigned in June 2022 and was charged with a class A [misdemeanor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misdemeanor "Misdemeanor") for animal abuse.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-37)

### Library resolution

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=St._Charles_County,_Missouri&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Library resolution")]

In 2023, the county council issued a resolution aimed at library policies and staff online activities. The resolution followed protests and comments at council meetings from residents who complained about a staff member wearing [gender non-conforming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender_non-conforming "Gender non-conforming") clothes. Within the resolution, the council asked the library CEO to remove an article they shared on their personal [LinkedIn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LinkedIn "LinkedIn") profile related to conservative campaigns targeting public libraries and [freedom of speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom_of_speech "Freedom of speech").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_County,_Missouri#cite_note-38)
