### Technology

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Technology")]

Efforts are under way to spur economic growth in South Bend. The St. Joe Valley Metronet is a 50-mile (80 km) dark fiber optic network that encircles South Bend and Mishawaka that allows for strong telecommunications connectivity.[[76]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-76) The South Bend Metronet, named Zing, is bringing more high-tech firms to the city and surrounding area. This telecommunications network has allowed for the advent of various data centers in South Bend, which serves as a hub between Chicago, Indianapolis, Detroit, and Cincinnati. In 2015, the City of South Bend announced it would provide free wireless internet access via the Metronet in the city's downtown and East Bank areas.[[77]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-77)

The [Union Station Technology Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Station_Technology_Center "Union Station Technology Center") was purchased from the city in 1979 and is currently Northern Indiana's largest data center.[[78]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-78) There are currently plans to extend the data center into a fully operating high-tech data hub in the old Studebaker "Ivy Tower" assembly plant next door, creating what will be called the Renaissance District.[[79]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-79)

#### Innovation Park and Ignition Park

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Innovation Park and Ignition Park")]

Innovation Park and Ignition Park, dual-certified technology parks, have attracted technology businesses to South Bend. Located across the street from the University of Notre Dame, Innovation Park was completed in 2009 and houses innovative researchers from companies and the university.[[80]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-80) Ignition Park, located just south of the downtown area, is planned to become home to 3 million square feet (280,000 m 2) of high-tech space on 140 acres (570,000 m 2) of land previously owned by the Studebaker Corporation.[[81]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-81) The first tenant, Data Realty, moved into the location in the fall of 2012.[[82]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-82) The second building in the new park, a research and testing facility for massive turbo machinery, is part of a partnership between the city, General Electric, Great Lakes Capital, Indiana Michigan Power, University of Notre Dame, and the state of Indiana.[[83]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-83)

### Redevelopment

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Redevelopment")]

Redevelopment is underway for some of the abandoned industrial facilities, with the abandoned [Oliver Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Corp. "Oliver Corp.") buildings being the most recent example of reclaimed property.[[84]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Reclaim-84) The city also faced programs with large swaths of vacant housing after the decline of the manufacturing industry. In 2013, 1,347 homes were vacant or abandoned.[[85]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-85) The city created the Vacant and Abandoned Properties Initiative in February 2013, which aimed to take care of 1,000 vacant or abandoned homes in 1,000 days, either through demolition, repairs, or some other satisfactory means.[[86]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-86)

The Smart Street Initiative, a 20-year plan to make the city safer for pedestrians, bicyclists, and motorists, began in 2013 with the conversion of one-way streets to two-way streets,[[87]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-87) to bring more businesses to the area, create shorter travel routes, and to reduce speeding. The other part of the initiative is the West Side Main Streets Plan, a revitalization plan for the Lincoln Way West and Western Avenue corridor focusing on guiding business owners, residents, and developers to improve the street front by offering a reimbursement on exterior improvements from the city and the Urban Enterprise Association.[[88]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-88)

## Arts and culture

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Arts and culture")]

### Culture

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Culture")]

South Bend was influenced by a large influx of [Polish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_people "Polish people")[Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Catholic_Church "Roman Catholic Church")[immigrants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immigrants "Immigrants") in the late 19th century.[[89]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-89)[Dyngus Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dyngus_Day "Dyngus Day") is widely celebrated on the Monday after [Easter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter "Easter") and it is the beginning of the city elections' [campaign season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_campaign "Political campaign").[[90]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-90)[Fat Tuesday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fat_Tuesday "Fat Tuesday") is also celebrated in South Bend, with _[paczkis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paczki "Paczki")_ being a staple food product in the city for the day.[[91]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-91) The city and surrounding county have 23 Catholic churches, 11 Catholic schools and three Catholic universities (the University of Notre Dame, Holy Cross College, and Saint Mary's College, all located in the adjacent unincorporated area of [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notre_Dame,_Indiana "Notre Dame, Indiana")).[[92]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-92)

### Music festivals

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Music festivals")]

[![Image 29: A local band, Interstate Traffic, performs outside the Morris Performing Arts Center in downtown South Bend as part of the "South By South Bend" music festival. Pictured are two members playing a drum set and an electric guitar.](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/63/Interstate_Traffic_SBSB.png/250px-Interstate_Traffic_SBSB.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Interstate_Traffic_SBSB.png)

Local band Interstate Traffic performing at South by South Bend

The city hosts several annual festivals. The South Bend International Festival began in 2004 as the South Bend Reggae Festival and now features local and international musical artists who perform in African, Latino, and American cultural styles. Proceeds from the festival are given to the Pangani Foundation of South Bend, which provides medical supplies to hospitals in [Malawi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malawi "Malawi"). The festival adopted its present name in 2014 on the tenth anniversary.[[93]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-93)

WBYT FM – B100 (Country Station) hosts an Annual All Day Country Concert, with over 37,000 free tickets in early September.

The World Pulse Festival, broadcast by LeSEA Broadcasting network, is held annually in South Bend. It is hosted by Pulse FM, a local Christian music radio station. The event is an annual [Contemporary Christian music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contemporary_Christian_music "Contemporary Christian music") festival, attracting more than 50,000 visitors each year.[[94]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-94)

In 2013, a new annual festival began in South Bend called South by South Bend, named after the famous South By Southwest of Austin, Texas. The festival is a celebration of the local music scene, with local bands and artists performing on the park grounds and other public venues around the city.[[95]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-95) The goals of the festival include strengthening the bond between the communities of South Bend and Notre Dame, supporting local artistic expression, and promoting local business.[[96]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-96) In 2015, the festival was renamed Sounds by South Bend, to avoid confusion with the Austin festival and to more accurately represent the purpose of the event.[[97]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-97) In 2016, the Riverlights Music Festival debuted as successor to Sounds by South Bend.[[98]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-98)

### Museums, arts and entertainment

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Museums, arts and entertainment")]

The [South Bend Museum of Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend_Museum_of_Art "South Bend Museum of Art") is located in [Century Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Century_Center_(South_Bend) "Century Center (South Bend)") in downtown South Bend. The museum was opened to the public in March 1996, and features a variety of artists from South Bend and the [Michiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michiana "Michiana") region. Currently, over 850 works are featured in the permanent collection. The museum also offers several classes and workshops for adults and children.[[99]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-museum-99)

#### The History Museum

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: The History Museum")]

The History Museum is the public name of the Northern Indiana Historical Society, the second-oldest historical society in Indiana, established in 1867 to collect and interpret the history of the northern Indiana region by St. Joseph County's leading citizens. [The Oliver Mansion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_D._Oliver_House "Joseph D. Oliver House") (also known by its original name, Copshaholm) is one of the central features of the museum. The 38-room mansion was built in 1895 and is currently listed in the [National Register of Historic Places](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places "National Register of Historic Places"). The home was built by Joseph Doty Oliver, son of James Oliver, the founder of the [Oliver Farm Equipment Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Farm_Equipment_Company "Oliver Farm Equipment Company"), once the largest plow manufacturer in the United States.[[100]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-CFH-100) In addition to the Oliver Mansion and the Workers Home (a 1920s Polish-American family home), the museum includes areas dedicated to the history of the St. Joseph River Valley, the University of Notre Dame, the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League, and the Kidsfirst Children's Museum.[[100]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-CFH-100)

#### Studebaker National Museum

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Studebaker National Museum")]

[![Image 30](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/50/South-bend-studebaker-museum-new.jpg/250px-South-bend-studebaker-museum-new.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:South-bend-studebaker-museum-new.jpg)

[Studebaker National Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker_National_Museum "Studebaker National Museum") in South Bend

The [Studebaker National Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker_National_Museum "Studebaker National Museum") holds a large collection of wagons and automobiles from the 150-year history of the [Studebaker Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker "Studebaker").[[101]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Stude-101) The museum began as a collection of wagons and automobiles produced by Studebaker, including the presidential carriages of Lincoln, McKinley, Harrison, and Grant. The company donated the collection to the city of South Bend in 1966. The collection was housed in various locations from [Century Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Century_Center_(South_Bend) "Century Center (South Bend)") to its current location in downtown South Bend, adjacent to The History Museum. The two museums share one campus, and together form [The Museums at Washington and Chapin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Museums_at_Washington_and_Chapin "The Museums at Washington and Chapin").[[102]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Chapin-102) The former South Bend mansion of [Clement Studebaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clement_Studebaker "Clement Studebaker"), named [Tippecanoe Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tippecanoe_Place "Tippecanoe Place"), is now a restaurant.

#### Indiana University Civil Rights Heritage Center

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Indiana University Civil Rights Heritage Center")]

The [Indiana University South Bend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_University_South_Bend "Indiana University South Bend")[Civil Rights Heritage Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Rights_Heritage_Center "Civil Rights Heritage Center") is housed in the former [Engman Public Natatorium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Engman_Public_Natatorium "Engman Public Natatorium"). What was once the city's first indoor swimming pool excluded and then segregated against African Americans for its first twenty-eight years. In 2010, Indiana University South Bend re-opened the building, and now offers tours and events focusing on the histories of civil rights and the experiences of African Americans, Latinos, and LGBTQ people in South Bend.

#### Theatrical buildings

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Theatrical buildings")]

[![Image 31](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0a/Palace_Theater%2C_Morris_Performing_Arts_Center%2C_in_South_Bend.jpg/250px-Palace_Theater%2C_Morris_Performing_Arts_Center%2C_in_South_Bend.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Palace_Theater,_Morris_Performing_Arts_Center,_in_South_Bend.jpg)

Morris Performing Arts Center in South Bend

The [Morris Performing Arts Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Performing_Arts_Center "Morris Performing Arts Center"), built in 1922, included the Palace Theater, a venue for [vaudeville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaudeville "Vaudeville"). The theatre's heyday was in 1940 with the premiere of _[Knute Rockne, All American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knute\_Rockne,\_All\_American "Knute Rockne, All American"),_ starring [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan"). A crowd estimated at 24,000 gathered outside. The theater was scheduled for demolition in 1959, when E. M. Morris purchased the facility and sold it to the city for one dollar, after which it was renamed the Morris Civic Auditorium. A total renovation as well as expansion of the stage area was completed in 2000. The Morris Performing Arts Center also includes the restored Palais Royale Ballroom.[[103]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-MorrisCenter-103) The center houses the Broadway Theater League and the South Bend Symphony Orchestra. The orchestra's Shanghai-born former conductor, [Tsung Yeh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsung_Yeh "Tsung Yeh"), was the first conductor ever to hold music directorships of both a western symphony orchestra and a major Chinese orchestra.[[104]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-South_Bend_Symphony_Orchestra-104)

South Bend is also home to The South Bend Hot Patooties, a group that performs a shadowcast of [The Rocky Horror Picture Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rocky_Horror_Picture_Show "The Rocky Horror Picture Show").[[105]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-105) The group has performed at various South Bend venues including the State Theater, Legends of Notre Dame, The Potawatomi Conservatories, and the historic [Birdsell Mansion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birdsell "Birdsell").[[106]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-106)

[South Bend Civic Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend_Civic_Theatre "South Bend Civic Theatre"), founded in 1957, was for many years located at The Firehouse, 701 Portage Avenue. It was a small intimate black box theater. In 2007, a new theater opened at 403 North Main Street in what was formerly the Scottish Rite Building. This facility includes a 209-seat main stage auditorium and a 90-seat "black box" studio theatre.[[107]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Civic_Theatre-107) The theater produces more than a dozen plays per year, including several productions in its Family Series.

### South Bend Lions FC

A [USL2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USL_League_Two "USL League Two")[soccer franchise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend_Lions_FC "South Bend Lions FC") named in November 2019, located in South Bend. ### South Bend Cubs

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=36 "Edit section: South Bend Cubs")]

See also: [South Bend, Indiana minor league baseball history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana_minor_league_baseball_history "South Bend, Indiana minor league baseball history")

The city is home to the [South Bend Cubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend_Cubs "South Bend Cubs"), a Class A [Minor League Baseball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minor_League_Baseball "Minor League Baseball") team, which plays at [Four Winds Field at Coveleski Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Four_Winds_Field_at_Coveleski_Stadium "Four Winds Field at Coveleski Stadium") in downtown South Bend. In 2014, the franchise changed its name and logo to the South Bend Cubs[[114]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-114) and became affiliated with the [Chicago Cubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Cubs "Chicago Cubs"); prior to this, it had been known as the South Bend Silver Hawks and affiliated with the [Arizona Diamondbacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Diamondbacks "Arizona Diamondbacks"). In 2005, the franchise nearly moved to [Marion, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marion,_Illinois "Marion, Illinois"), but a group of investors, led by former Indiana governor and former South Bend mayor [Joe Kernan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Kernan_(politician) "Joe Kernan (politician)"), bought the Silver Hawks in order to ensure the team stayed in South Bend.[[46]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Hawks-46)

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=37 "Edit section: Buildings and stadium")]

### South Bend Roller Girls

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=38 "Edit section: South Bend Roller Girls")]

The city also hosts the South Bend Roller Girls,[[118]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-118) the city's non-profit flat-track roller derby league. ### East Race Waterway

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=39 "Edit section: East Race Waterway")]

Main article: [East Race Waterway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Race_Waterway "East Race Waterway")

South Bend is home to the first [artificial whitewater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_whitewater "Artificial whitewater") center in North America, the [East Race Waterway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Race_Waterway "East Race Waterway"), adjacent to Century Center. The East Race Waterway is one of only four operating artificial whitewater facilities in the United States, the others being [Dickerson Whitewater Course](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickerson_Whitewater_Course "Dickerson Whitewater Course") (in [Dickerson, Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dickerson,_Maryland "Dickerson, Maryland")), [U.S. National Whitewater Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._National_Whitewater_Center "U.S. National Whitewater Center") (in [Charlotte, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte,_North_Carolina "Charlotte, North Carolina")), [Adventure Sports Center International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adventure_Sports_Center_International "Adventure Sports Center International") (in [McHenry, Maryland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McHenry,_Maryland "McHenry, Maryland")), and [Riversports Rapids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riversports_Rapids?action=edit&redlink=1 "Riversports Rapids (page does not exist)") (in [Oklahoma City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City "Oklahoma City"), [Oklahoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma "Oklahoma")). The East Race Waterway is one of only [six such facilities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_artificial_whitewater_courses "List of artificial whitewater courses") to have ever been operated in the US, the others being the four aforementioned courses and the now-defunct [Ocoee Whitewater Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocoee_Whitewater_Center "Ocoee Whitewater Center") (in [Ducktown, Tennessee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ducktown,_Tennessee "Ducktown, Tennessee")). Prior to the opening of Riversports Rapids, the East Race had long been the only such US facility not located in an [East Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Coast_of_the_United_States "East Coast of the United States") state. The waterway is closed as of 2021 because a [hydroelectric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydroelectric "Hydroelectric")[dam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dam "Dam") is being built at the source.[[119]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-119)

Rafters enjoying the East Race in South Bend, Indiana

South Bend Parks and Recreation department operates over 50 parks, golf courses, and recreational areas throughout the city.[[122]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Rec-122) Notable parks include Rum Village Park, which has a disc golf course, mountain bike trails, hiking trails, and a nature center,[[123]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Rum-123) and Potawatomi Park, which has the region's largest Universally Accessible Playground and an outdoors Performance Arts Pavilion and viewing area.[[124]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Area-124)

South Bend's first zoo was located at Leeper Park from 1902 until 1914. The present zoo at Potawatomi Park began in 1921 when Albert R. Erskine, the president of the Studebaker Corporation, donated a single deer as the start of the zoo. The [Potawatomi Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potawatomi_Zoo "Potawatomi Zoo") is the second oldest zoo in Indiana. It features more than 400 animals in its 23 acres (93,000 m 2). The zoo is now operated by the Potawatomi Zoological Society.

Near the Potawatomi Zoo are the [Potawatomi Greenhouses and the Ella Morris and Muessel-Ellison Botanical Conservatories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potawatomi_Conservatories "Potawatomi Conservatories"). The greenhouses were originally constructed in the 1920s, with the conservatories added in the 1960s.[[125]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-greenhouse-125) In 2007, the greenhouses and conservatories were in danger of closing due to increased operating costs, but a campaign by the Botanical Society of South Bend was able to raise funds to keep the facilities operating.[[126]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-erace-126)

The city is home to the [East Race Waterway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Race_Waterway "East Race Waterway"), which is used for boating and water sports (see above).[[126]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-erace-126)

While developing the 2006 City Plan, the city's 20-year comprehensive plan, citizens said the encouragement of bicycling as a form of alternative transportation was a top priority. In 2010, South Bend became one of 303 communities in the United States to be recognized as a "Bicycle-Friendly Community" by the League of American Bicyclists due to the city's "remarkable commitments to bicycling.[[127]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-bike-127) The city has developed a long-term plan for building a 116-mile (187 km) South Bend Bikeway network. As of late 2014[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit), 66.8 miles (107.5 km) of bicycle routes have been established, including 17.4 miles (28.0 km) of multipurpose paths separated from streets, 17.0 miles (27.4 km) of striped bike lanes, and 32.4 miles (52.1 km) of on-street routes bearing other designations.[[128]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-southbike-128) The area is also served by the St. Joseph County Parks Dept, which maintains eight different parks and recreation areas. The Parks department serves the metro area and is headed by a permanent staff and an appointed board.

South Bend government follows the [mayor-council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor-council "Mayor-council")[representative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representative_democracy "Representative democracy") model of [municipal government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipal_government "Municipal government") and, along with the St. Joseph county government, occupies the County-City Building in downtown South Bend.

The government of South Bend is led by the office of the [mayor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor "Mayor"), who is elected to a four-year term and acts as chief executive for the city government. The current mayor is [James Mueller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Mueller_(mayor) "James Mueller (mayor)").

The legislative branch of the South Bend government is the [South Bend Common Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend_Common_Council "South Bend Common Council").

**South Bend** is a city in [St. Joseph County, Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_County,_Indiana "St. Joseph County, Indiana"), United States, and its [county seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_seat "County seat").[[7]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-GR6-7) It lies along the [St. Joseph River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_River_(Lake_Michigan) "St. Joseph River (Lake Michigan)") near its southernmost bend, from which it derives its name. It is the [fourth-most populous city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Indiana "List of cities in Indiana") in Indiana with a population of 103,453 at the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"). Located directly south of Indiana's northern border with [Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan "Michigan"), South Bend anchors the broader [Michiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michiana "Michiana") region. Its [metropolitan area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend-Mishawaka_metropolitan_area "South Bend-Mishawaka metropolitan area") had a population of 324,501 in 2020, while its combined statistical area had 812,199 residents.[[8]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-8)

The area was first settled in the early 19th century by [fur traders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fur_trade "Fur trade") and was established as a city in 1865.[[9]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-9) The St. Joseph River shaped South Bend's economy through the mid-20th century. River access assisted heavy industrial development such as that of the [Studebaker Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker "Studebaker") and the [Oliver Chilled Plow Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Corporation "Oliver Corporation").

Like other [Rust Belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_Belt "Rust Belt") cities, South Bend has been affected by population and industrial decline since the 1960s. This has been chiefly due to the demise of Studebaker, migration to suburban areas, and the loss of other [heavy industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_industry "Heavy industry"). However, in recent years, there have been successful efforts to invest in and revitalize blighted areas of the city. Today, the largest industries in South Bend are health care, education, small business, and tourism. The city is home to manufacturer [AM General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AM_General "AM General") and financial services company [1st Source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Source "1st Source"). A major draw for visitors is the nearby [University of Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Notre_Dame "University of Notre Dame"), which also plays an important role in the local economy and culture.

The city is served by the [South Bend International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend_International_Airport "South Bend International Airport") and by the [South Shore Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Shore_Line "South Shore Line") commuter railway, connecting South Bend to [downtown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Loop "Chicago Loop")[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), which is 72 miles (116 km) to the west.

## History

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Early history

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early history")]

The St. Joseph Valley was long occupied by Native Americans. One of the earliest known groups to occupy what would later become northern Indiana was the [Miami tribe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_tribe "Miami tribe"). Later, the [Potawatomi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potawatomi "Potawatomi") moved into the region, utilizing the rich food and natural resources found along the river. The Potawatomi occupied this region of Indiana until most of them were forcibly removed in the 1840s. The South Bend area was popular because its portage was the shortest overland route from the St. Joseph River to the [Kankakee River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kankakee_River "Kankakee River").[[10]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-10) This route was used for centuries, first by the Native Americans, then by French explorers, missionaries and traders.[[11]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-11) The French explorer René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle, the first white European to set foot in what is now South Bend,[[12]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-12) used this portage between the St. Joseph River and the Kankakee River in December 1679.

### First settlements

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: First settlements")]

The first permanent white settlers of South Bend were fur traders who established trading posts in the area. In 1820, [Pierre Frieschutz Navarre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Frieschutz_Navarre?action=edit&redlink=1 "Pierre Frieschutz Navarre (page does not exist)") arrived, representing the [American Fur Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Fur_Company "American Fur Company") (AFC) of [John Jacob Astor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jacob_Astor "John Jacob Astor"). He settled near what is now downtown South Bend.[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Crossroads-13)[Alexis Coquillard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Coquillard "Alexis Coquillard"), another agent of the AFC,[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Crossroads-13)[[14]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-StHistory-14) established a trading post known as the Big St. Joseph Station.[[15]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-15) In 1827, [Lathrop Minor Taylor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lathrop_Minor_Taylor?action=edit&redlink=1 "Lathrop Minor Taylor (page does not exist)") established a post for Samuel Hanna and Company, in whose records the name St. Joseph's, Indiana was used.[[14]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-StHistory-14) By 1829, the town was growing, with Coquillard and Taylor emerging as leaders. They applied for a post office. Taylor was appointed [postmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postmaster "Postmaster"), and the post office was designated as Southold, Allen County, Indiana.[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Crossroads-13) The following year, the name was changed to South Bend, probably to ease confusion, as several other communities were named Southold at the time.

In 1831, South Bend was laid out as the county seat and as one of the four original townships of [St. Joseph County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_County,_Indiana "St. Joseph County, Indiana") with 128 residents.[[16]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-16) That same year, [Horatio Chapin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horatio_Chapin "Horatio Chapin") moved to the settlement, opened the first general store with imported (out of state) goods and helped established the first church and Sunday school.[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Crossroads-13) Around the same time, design began on what would become the town of South Bend. The town was formally established in 1835, with Chapin as the first president of the board of town trustees.[[17]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-17) In 1856, attorney Andrew Anderson, Chapin's son-in-law, founded May Oberfell Lorber, the oldest continuous business in St. Joseph County.[[18]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-18) He compiled a complete index of South Bend's real estate records.[[19]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-19)

[![Image 23](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Alexis-Coquillard.jpg/250px-Alexis-Coquillard.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Alexis-Coquillard.jpg)

[Alexis Coquillard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexis_Coquillard "Alexis Coquillard")

In 1841, [Schuyler Colfax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schuyler_Colfax "Schuyler Colfax") was appointed St. Joseph County deputy auditor. Colfax purchased the _South Bend Free Press_ and then turned it into a pro-[Whig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whig_Party_(United_States) "Whig Party (United States)") newspaper, the _St. Joseph Valley Register_. He was a member of the state constitutional convention of 1850, at which he opposed the barring of African American migration to Indiana. He joined the [Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)"), like many Whigs of his day, and was elected to Congress in 1855, becoming Speaker of the House in 1863 during the administration of [Abraham Lincoln](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln "Abraham Lincoln"). In 1868, he was elected vice president under [Ulysses S. Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulysses_S._Grant "Ulysses S. Grant"). Colfax returned to South Bend after his stint in Washington and is buried in City Cemetery, west of downtown.[[20]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-20)

### Early business

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Early business")]

During the late 1830s through the 1850s, much of South Bend's development centered on the industrial complex of factories located on the two [races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mill_race "Mill race") (man-made canals along the [St. Joseph River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_River_(Lake_Michigan) "St. Joseph River (Lake Michigan)") in South Bend). Several dams were created and factories were built on each side of the river. On October 4, 1851, the first steam [locomotive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Locomotive "Locomotive") entered South Bend.[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Crossroads-13) This shifted commerce from the river to the [railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Railroad "Railroad"). In 1852, Henry Studebaker set up [Studebaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker "Studebaker") wagon shop, later becoming the world's largest wagon builder and the only one to later succeed as an automobile manufacturer. The [Singer Sewing Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singer_Corporation "Singer Corporation") and the [Oliver Chilled Plow Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Corporation "Oliver Corporation") were among other companies that made manufacturing the driving force in the South Bend economy until the mid-20th century.[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Crossroads-13) Another important economic act was the dredging of the [Kankakee River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kankakee_River "Kankakee River") in 1884 to create farmland.[[21]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-21) During this time period there was a great immigration of Europeans, such as Polish, Hungarian, Irish, German, Italian, and Swedish people to South Bend because of available employment in area factories.[[22]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-22)

[![Image 24](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/36/South-Bend-1866.gif/250px-South-Bend-1866.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:South-Bend-1866.gif)

South Bend in 1866

South Bend benefited from its location on the [Michigan Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_Road "Michigan Road"), the main north–south artery of [northern Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Indiana "Northern Indiana") in the 19th century.[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Crossroads-13) Another significant development occurred near South Bend in 1842, when Father [Edward Sorin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Sorin "Edward Sorin") founded the [University of Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Notre_Dame "University of Notre Dame") just north of the town.[[23]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-ND-23) It became a major factor in the area's economy and culture.[[24]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-NDEcon-24)

### Establishment and early history

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Establishment and early history")]

South Bend was incorporated as a city on May 22, 1865, and its first elections were held on June 5, 1865, with William G. George elected as its first mayor[[14]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-StHistory-14) The official city motto, "Peace", refers to the fact that incorporation came in the month following the [Confederate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederate_States_of_America "Confederate States of America") surrender that effectively ended the [American Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Civil_War "American Civil War").

Industrial growth was rapid after the Civil War, most notably with the [Studebaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker "Studebaker") wagon factory, and the [Oliver plow company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oliver_Farm_Equipment_Company "Oliver Farm Equipment Company"). Good jobs and high wages attracted immigrants from Europe, especially Germans, Irish, and Poles. The majority were Catholic, and they achieved higher rates of social mobility than the same ethnic groups in the Northeast.[[25]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-25)

Olivet African Methodist Episcopal (AME) Church was founded in South Bend in March 1870, making it the first African American church in the city.[[26]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-26) Olivet AME is still an active African Methodist Episcopal Church, and celebrated its 145th anniversary in 2015.[[27]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-27)

A sergeant from South Bend fired the first American shells against Germany in World War I.[[28]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-28)

#### History with Ku Klux Klan

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: History with Ku Klux Klan")]

In 1923, the African American owner of a soda fountain received a letter signed "KKK", threatening to kill an African American man held in the city's jail and harm the rest of the city's African American population. Within a few days, over a thousand African Americans fled the city.[[29]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-29)

In 1924, the [Ku Klux Klan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ku_Klux_Klan "Ku Klux Klan") held a conference and planned a parade from its local headquarters at 230 S. Michigan St. In preparation, Klan members were posted around town to direct traffic. Students from the nearby [University of Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Notre_Dame "University of Notre Dame"), aware of the anti-Catholic nature of the Klan, vigorously protested this intrusion, and before noon all of the Klansmen traffic directors had been "unmasked and unrobed." Notre Dame students continued the fight, with several hundred gathering outside of the Klan headquarters, throwing rocks and smashing windows in protest. Local police as well as Notre Dame officials eventually managed to convince them to return to campus.[[30]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-30)[[31]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-31)[[32]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-32)[[33]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-33) Notre Dame football coach and athletic director [Knute Rockne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knute_Rockne "Knute Rockne") became involved in the struggle to calm down the students.[[34]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-34)

### Later business

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Later business")]

Other companies in the manufacturing industry developed in South Bend in the early 20th century, including Birdsell Manufacturing Company, the [Bendix Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bendix_Corporation "Bendix Corporation"), [Honeywell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeywell "Honeywell"), [AlliedSignal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AlliedSignal "AlliedSignal"), [South Bend Lathe Works](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend_Lathe_Works "South Bend Lathe Works"), the O'Brien Paint Corp., the South Bend Toy Company, South Bend Range, South Bend Bait Company, and [South Bend Watch Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend_Watch_Company "South Bend Watch Company"). Workers at the [Bendix Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bendix_Corporation "Bendix Corporation") staged the first sit-in strike in American history in 1936.[[35]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-35) Fast development led to the creation of [electric rail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Railway_electrification_system "Railway electrification system") transportation throughout the area, and in 1925, the [South Shore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Shore_Line "South Shore Line")[interurban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interurban "Interurban") service was established from downtown South Bend to downtown Chicago.[[36]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-rail-36) The South Shore Line still runs daily to and from Chicago and also is a major freight carrier in the area.

On June 30, 1934, the Merchants National Bank in South Bend was the last bank to be robbed by the [Dillinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Dillinger "John Dillinger") gang.[[37]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-37)

[![Image 25](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/South_Bend%2C_World_Famed.jpg/250px-South_Bend%2C_World_Famed.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:South_Bend,_World_Famed.jpg)

This 1922 pamphlet demonstrates the visions of progress and global importance in the peak period of industrialization in South Bend.

### Recent history

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Recent history")]

On September 29, 1929, South Bend completed its "track elevation program".[[38]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-trackelevration-38) This was a railroad infrastructure project which saw the removal of [Grand Trunk Western Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Trunk_Western_Railroad "Grand Trunk Western Railroad") tracks from Division Street, the removal of [level crossings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Level_crossing "Level crossing") from Chapin to Miami streets, the creation of a modern freight layout, and the construction of [Union Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union_Station_(South_Bend,_Indiana) "Union Station (South Bend, Indiana)").[[38]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-trackelevration-38) This project had been seventeen years in the making,[[38]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-trackelevration-38) and had been the subject of the [Indiana Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Supreme_Court "Indiana Supreme Court") case Vandalia Railroad v. South Bend, which was subsequently affirmed by the [Supreme Court of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States").[[38]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-trackelevration-38)[[39]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-39)

In 1949, percussionist [Lionel Hampton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Hampton "Lionel Hampton") was informed that his concert at South Bend's Palais du Royale would be a blacks-only event; he threatened to call for a boycott of the venue, and the affair proceeded as an integrated evening, which newspapers said led to all attendees breaking out in "paroxysms of ecstasy".[[40]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-40)

By 1950, more than half of all employment was in the manufacturing sector.[[41]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-EconMan-41) Due to economic difficulties, [Studebaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker "Studebaker") closed its automotive manufacturing plants in South Bend in December 1963.[[42]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-EarlyHist-42) A general decline in manufacturing soon followed as industry was restructured nationwide. By 2000, only 16% of the local economy consisted of manufacturing. Due to the severe loss of jobs, the city's population decreased by nearly 30,000 during that period.[[41]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-EconMan-41) This decline of industry and population loss led to the area being designated as part of the midwestern [Rust Belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_Belt "Rust Belt") due to the effects of [deindustrialization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deindustrialization "Deindustrialization").[[43]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-43)

In 1984, South Bend community leaders began seeking a minor-league baseball team for the city. A stadium was constructed in 1986 and a 10-year player-development contract was signed with the [Chicago White Sox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_White_Sox "Chicago White Sox"). The team would be known as the South Bend White Sox. In 1994, the team's name was changed to the South Bend Silver Hawks,[[44]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-SilverHawks-44) and then to the [South Bend Cubs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend_Cubs "South Bend Cubs") in 2015. They are a Class A minor league affiliate of the Chicago Cubs in the Midwest League.

In 2015, the City of South Bend celebrated its 150th birthday. The yearlong festival culminated with the ceremonial illumination of the first [River Lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/River_Lights "River Lights") along the St. Joseph River, and included appearances by Mayor [Pete Buttigieg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Buttigieg "Pete Buttigieg") along with five previous South Bend mayors: [Steve Luecke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Luecke "Steve Luecke"), [Joe Kernan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Kernan_(politician) "Joe Kernan (politician)"), [Roger Parent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Parent_(mayor) "Roger Parent (mayor)"), [Peter Nemeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nemeth "Peter Nemeth"), and Jerry Miller.[[45]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-45)

In 2015, the city's population increased by 286, the largest one-year growth in over twenty years.[[46]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Hawks-46) The former [Studebaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker "Studebaker") plant has been developed as the [Ignition Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ignition_Park "Ignition Park") center to attract new businesses, especially in the tech industry.[[47]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-:0-47) South Bend has also seen new development, particularly in the tech field, a decline in unemployment, and a renewal of the downtown area under Buttigieg's tenure, which has been described as a revival and South Bend as a 'turnaround city'.[[48]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-48)[[49]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-49)[[50]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-50)[[51]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-51)[[52]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-52) South Bend also was in the national spotlight during the 2019-20 Democratic presidential campaign of former mayor Buttigieg.

## Geography

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Geography")]

[![Image 26](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/South-bend-indiana.jpg/250px-South-bend-indiana.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:South-bend-indiana.jpg)

An aerial photo of Downtown South Bend, with the Notre Dame campus and the Indiana Toll Road in the background

South Bend is located 5 mi (8 km) from the [Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan "Michigan") border and approximately equidistant from [Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois "Illinois") and [Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio "Ohio"). The city is 93 mi (150 km) from Chicago. The shore of [Lake Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Michigan "Lake Michigan") is 20 mi (32 km) away.

According to the 2010 census, South Bend has a total area of 41.877 square miles (108.46 km 2), of which 41.46 square miles (107.38 km 2), or 99%, is land and 0.417 square miles (1.08 km 2), or 1%, is water.[[53]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-census-g001-53)

### Cityscape

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Cityscape")]

The [St. Joseph River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Joseph_River_(Lake_Michigan) "St. Joseph River (Lake Michigan)") flows from the east end of the city turning north near the city center, giving South Bend its name at the bend in the river. South Bend is located on the north–south continental divide, and the river flows northwest into Lake Michigan.[[54]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-climate-54) The downtown area is located in the north-central part of the city along the St. Joseph River. [Notre Dame, Indiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notre_Dame,_Indiana "Notre Dame, Indiana"), is directly adjacent to the north. The city extends further north on the west side, mainly with manufacturing and distribution facilities near the [South Bend International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend_International_Airport "South Bend International Airport"). [Mishawaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mishawaka "Mishawaka"), Indiana, is adjacent to South Bend's east side.

### Neighborhoods

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Neighborhoods")]

Notable neighborhoods in the city include:

*   Far Northwest, Near Northwest, and Keller Park are located off of Portage Avenue along the riverfront.
*   Northeast South Bend is between the River and [SR 23](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_State_Road_23 "Indiana State Road 23") north of East LaSalle Avenue.
*   River Park is located north and south of Mishawaka Avenue. It has been the subject of several redevelopment projects intended to revitalize the area.[[55]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-55)[[56]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-56)
*   The Wayne Street neighborhood between Washington Street and Sunnymede Avenue along Jefferson Boulevard was designated a historic district in 1987.[[57]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-57)
*   Rum Village is in Southwest South Bend north of West Ewing Avenue and west of South Main Street.
*   The Eddy Street Commons is a mixed-use complex along North Eddy Street across Angela Boulevard from [Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Notre_Dame "University of Notre Dame").
*   Leeper Park is south of the River and northwest of the [Memorial Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorial_Hospital_of_South_Bend "Memorial Hospital of South Bend") main campus.
*   The North Shore Triangle is located in between Angela Boulevard and North Shore Drive, just across the river from Leeper Park[[58]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-58)

### Climate

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Climate")]

South Bend has a [humid continental climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_continental_climate "Humid continental climate"), with a [Köppen climate classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") of _Dfa_. Lake Michigan exerts a great influence on the climate of South Bend, including [lake-effect snow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake-effect_snow "Lake-effect snow") in winter and a tendency to moderate temperatures year round.[[59]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-climate3-59) June, July and August are the warmest months, with average temperatures above 69°F (21°C). Normally, 42 days with [thunderstorms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thunderstorms "Thunderstorms") occur each year.[[59]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-climate3-59) The snowiest month is usually January, with snowfall normally recorded from October through April.[[60]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-climate2-60) On average, South Bend receives 64.5 inches (164 cm) of snow per year.[[59]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-climate3-59) Spring and fall can be mild and overcast, but also severely stormy at times with 293 partly cloudy to cloudy days each year.[[61]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-climate4-61)

### 2010 census

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

As of the [census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census "Census")[[69]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-wwwcensusgov-69) of 2010, there were 101,168 people, 39,760 households, and 23,526 families residing in the city. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 2,440.1 inhabitants per square mile (942.1/km 2). There were 46,324 housing units at an average density of 1,117.3 per square mile (431.4/km 2). The racial makeup of the city was 60.5% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 26.6% [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)"), 0.5% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 1.3% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.1% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), 6.9% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(U.S._Census) "Race (U.S. Census)"), and 4.2% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") residents of any race were 13.0% of the population.

There were 39,760 households, of which 33.1% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 34.9% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 18.9% had a female householder with no husband present, 5.4% had a male householder with no wife present, and 40.8% were non-families. 33.3% Of all households were made up of individuals, and 11.4% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.48 and the average family size was 3.19.

The median age in the city was 33.3 years. 27.3% of residents were under the age of 18; 10% were between the ages of 18 and 24; 27.1% were from 25 to 44; 23.1% were from 45 to 64; and 12.5% were 65 years of age or older. The gender makeup of the city was 48.4% male and 51.6% female.

## Economy

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Economy")]

[![Image 28](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Liberty-Tower-SB_IMG_1486_7-17-2020.jpg/250px-Liberty-Tower-SB_IMG_1486_7-17-2020.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Liberty-Tower-SB_IMG_1486_7-17-2020.jpg)

25-story [Liberty Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Tower_(South_Bend) "Liberty Tower (South Bend)"), the tallest building in South Bend

South Bend's location on the St. Joseph River led to an industrial-based economy in the late 19th century and early-to-mid-20th century. In 1923, industrialist and entrepreneur [Vincent H. Bendix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Hugo_Bendix "Vincent Hugo Bendix") selected South Bend as the site of his new manufacturing plant for automotive parts.[[71]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Hallett,_Anthony_1997_p._51-71) He chose South Bend primarily because it was on a rail line midway between Chicago and Detroit, the two automotive manufacturing centers of the United States at the time.[[71]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-Hallett,_Anthony_1997_p._51-71) Eventually, the Bendix corporation built a vast manufacturing complex on its South Bend acreage served by the major railroads, including a huge shipping and receiving building where railroad cars could enter at one end, unload, and depart at the opposite end.

By the end of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), manufacturing began to diminish.[[72]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-industry-72) The [Studebaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker "Studebaker") plant, which had at one time employed 45,000 persons, [closed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studebaker#Exit_from_auto_business "Studebaker") in 1963; its engine block plant shuttered the following year. Parts of the Bendix factory complex were later acquired and divided between [Honeywell Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeywell_Corporation "Honeywell Corporation") and [Bosch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Bosch_GmbH "Robert Bosch GmbH") Corporation, respectively. Honeywell Aerospace continues to manufacture aviation products at its former Bendix facility. In 2010, Bosch announced that it would cease all operations at its [Bendix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bendix_Corporation "Bendix Corporation") plant location in South Bend by the end of 2011.[[73]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-73) Bosch vacated the building entirely in October 2012. Curtis Products of South Bend moved into the building in May 2013.

### Employers

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=South_Bend,_Indiana&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Employers")]

Since the 1960s, education, health care, and small business have come to the forefront of South Bend's economy, though the city has never regained the level of prosperity it enjoyed before that time. Nearby [University of Notre Dame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Notre_Dame "University of Notre Dame") is a large contributor to the local economy. The university is the second-largest employer in the city and in St. Joseph County, employing 6,086 people.[[74]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-comprehensive-74)

Health care is another major contributor to the South Bend economy. In 2012, [Memorial Health System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorial_Health_System "Memorial Health System") announced that it was merging with Elkhart General Hospital, located in Elkhart County, to form Beacon Health System.[[75]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-75) Beacon is the largest employer in the city and in St. Joseph County, employing 7,088 people.[[74]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_Indiana#cite_note-comprehensive-74) Other notable businesses include [Honeywell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honeywell "Honeywell"), Bosch, and [PEI Genesis.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PEI-Genesis.?action=edit&redlink=1 "PEI-Genesis.
